section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

title: Issue nonhuman agent principals and current context grants
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Agent service identity, sponsor, invoker/delegation, tenant/entity, purpose, audience, and source/capability grants intersect and are rechecked at tool and delivery boundaries

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Accessible draft steps show charter, context, tools, triggers, budgets, authority preview, sandbox evidence, exact review digest, publication status, and owner transfer

title: Ship versioned starting templates for business agents
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Policy Guide and one second pilot template create tenant-owned drafts with pinned template provenance; grants still require validation, authority preview, evaluation, and publication

green: Previewed rollout plans create revisioned per-conversation installations; manager approval and current membership/classification gates each admission, suspension, and removal
refactor: Keep rollout reconciliation separate from chat-owned membership and post storage

title: Admit one idempotent AgentRunRequest across all invocation modes
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: A replay creates two runs or an API, schedule, or workflow entry point skips version, sponsor, purpose, audience, deadline, or budget checks
green: One admission contract persists accepted or refused requests by source key and pins agent version, principal chain, context scope, deadline, budget, and cause ID before inference
refactor: Keep entry-point adapters thin and all authority in the shared admission service

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: Worker death loses an admitted run, replays a side-effecting tool, or leaves cancellation and expiry without terminal state
green: Leased workers checkpoint admission, context, model, tool, validation, and delivery steps; restart reconciles ambiguous effects and reaches one typed terminal outcome
refactor: Keep model attempts and business effects as distinct durable records

title: Build current EffectiveAgentContext from owning services
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: A chat message supplies tenant or role, stale HCM facts are presented as current, or a source grant revoked mid-run survives delivery
green: Context carries tenant/entity, purpose, principal chain, temporal mode, source provenance and freshness, classification, audience, policy versions, and revocation tokens with late rechecks

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: A citation reveals a hidden document or channel, a removed member retains context, or adapter failure is treated as a negative business fact
green: Typed retrieval envelopes carry owner, version, classification, audience, purpose, freshness, citation, and revocation; partial failure is explicit and current grants govern final disclosure

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: Provider response IDs or hosted sessions become authoritative run memory, or unsupported tool/output modes pass as equivalent
green: One versioned ModelRequest/ModelResult schema records policy, model profile, tools, output, limits, usage, finish and errors; adapters advertise supported features and return typed refusals

title: Gate provider egress, credentials, retention, and data class
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Adapter maps request, proposed tools, usage, finish, errors, cancellation, and streaming to the owned contract; HCM Next alone executes admitted tools

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Approved endpoint profile declares network path, identity, model/tool/output support, processing policy, health and limits; conformance yields the same HCM decisions

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

title: Bridge model tool proposals to typed capability execution
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: Unknown tool, forged arguments, parallel-call burst, or source text can add a tool, broaden scope, or execute an effect

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: A partial stream, hidden citation, private fact, unknown card field, or stale grant reaches a public post or workflow result
green: Complete output is schema/citation/taint checked and reauthorized for every current recipient and destination immediately before commit; unsafe output refuses or routes privately

title: Invoke owned agents from chat DMs, mentions, and slash commands
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration
red: Quoted mention runs an agent, a user invokes an uninstalled agent, or provider failure blocks the original chat post

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Versioned target kind AGENT_RUN binds schedule, exact agent version, sponsor, purpose, budget and destination while legacy intent targets retain their semantics

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Owner drafts and previews recurrence, timezone/calendar, DST/misfire/overlap, pinned version, recipient grant and budget; reviewer publishes and controls pause, skip, resume, and dry-run

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Schedule outbox and agent dedupe inbox reconcile at least once delivery by tenant/schedule/revision/occurrence/version key; current grants and pause recheck before work

section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

green: Published event classes expose audience-filtered projections with subscription version, debounce, dedupe, cause depth, budget and revocation

title: Invoke an agent as a workflow CAPABILITY and resume by typed signal
section: 87. Customer-owned agent runtime and business integration

evidence: `TestConcreteSelectionConvergenceSecondPassProducesNoNewGapIdentity` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus `TestTodo_CLOSE_002_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Fault`, `_Security`, `_Conformance` and `_Mutation`, `TestRunToFixedPointDetectsReproposal` and `TestRunToFixedPointDetectsAnImpureCompiler` in the new `tools/planning/convergence`; `tools/planning/cmd/convergence`'s own tests; `TestScanTestNamesIncludesTheTestRoot` and `TestLoadSnapshotSeesEveryLiveTestRootSuite` in `tools/planning/designclosure` and `TestScanRepoTestNamesIncludesTheTestRoot` in `tools/planning/intentcoverage`; no migration. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 95.3% (`convergence`), 89.0% (`cmd/convergence`), 94.1% (`designclosure`, whose `loader.go` had no test before) and 90.0% (`intentcoverage`), with `workflowmaturity`, `closurewitness` and `intentcoverage/cmd/intentcoverage` re-run green by the orchestrator after the loader change; gofmt, vet and staticcheck clean (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. Every selected gap must resolve to an open claiming todo (a claim from a ticked or retired todo is refused and reported), a proposed `CONV-xxxxxxxx` todo whose id, owner, phase and test name are pure functions of the gap key, or a rejection carrying both rationale and a named decider. Twelve lane mutations failed by name, and an orchestrator mutation removing the subject from `GapIdentity` independently failed Golden, Conformance and three unit tests. title: Freeze the pilot package, pricing hypothesis and contractual authority boundary
section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: package promises unselected intent/provider/jurisdiction/SLO, confuses overlay authority with system-of-record ownership, omits implementation/support/provider cost, bills replay/repair duplicates, lacks data processing/retention/exit terms or hides hypothesis/stop threshold
green: signed package maps entitlements and exclusions to the Phase 1 digest, declares price/usage/support/implementation assumptions, legal/authority boundaries, provider pass-throughs, evidence/SLOs, termination/export obligations and quantitative reprice/stop criteria
refactor: commercial views consume entitlement, usage, cost and release registries; contract prose cannot independently enable capability
evidence: `TestPilotCommercialPackageMatchesReleaseEntitlementsCostsRisksAndExitTerms` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus the `_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Security`, `_Conformance` and `_Mutation` tests, `TestReplayAndRepairEventsAreNeverBilled`, `TestConformsToLiveRegistriesCatchesADivergingFreeze` and the ceiling-authorization refactor test in `tools/planning/pilotcommercial`, and `tools/planning/cmd/pilotcommercial`'s own tests; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.5% (`tools/planning/pilotcommercial`) and 79.6% (`tools/planning/cmd/pilotcommercial`), both above the floor; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The freeze is `definitions/planning/gates/commercial-001-pilot-package.yaml`. **RED's first clause -- that the package must not promise an unselected intent, provider, jurisdiction or SLO -- is the spine of this todo and is satisfied by derivation rather than assertion.** The eight P1A entitlements and four exclusions are pinned field-for-field to `internal/commercial.DefaultPilotCommercialPackage()` and each entitlement is independently checked against `PHASE-001`'s live scope ceiling for an `INCLUDE` disposition. Jurisdiction is `SELECTED_PENDING_REVIEW` for US/CA with `review_status: UNREVIEWED`, cross-checked live against `SELECT-001`'s profile, with `legal.ParseReviewStatus(...).Releasable()` deciding whether `SELECTED_CONFIRMED` could ever be legal -- it is not, today. Provider is `status: NONE` with no vendor reference, cross-checked live against `SELECT-002`'s topology through `SatisfiesRealProviderSelectionGate()`, which is false today, making `NONE` the only legal value. SLO is `NONE`, bound to `PHASE-001`'s `slo` selection slot, which names `SELECT-002, COMMERCIAL-001` as joint fillers and remains `filled: false`: **COMMERCIAL-001 fills its half by promising nothing, and never by editing the ceiling**, which that ceiling's own security test would detect as a signature violation anyway. Pricing is mirrored from the live registry with `pricing.is_hypothesis: true`, matching the todo's own framing of a pricing hypothesis rather than an agreed rate card. Authority declares zero owned domains, `write_authority: false` and an `EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION` topology, so the package claims overlay authority and never system-of-record ownership; `Validate` rejects any domain claimed as both owned and observed, any owned domain lacking write authority, and any `EXTERNAL_OBSERVATION` topology carrying write authority or owned domains. RED's replay and repair clause is enforced rather than declared: `BillingPolicy` closes `replay_billable` and `repair_billable` to false and `ComputeBillableTotal` skips any replay or repair event regardless of idempotency key while separately deduplicating duplicate `NEW` submissions by key. The test fixture deliberately contains both a shared-key and an isolated-key replay and repair so the kind check is proven to fire independently of key-based deduplication -- **a first version of that fixture was masked by the dedup and had to be strengthened**, which is exactly the vacuous-fixture trap. `ConformsToLiveRegistries` re-reads the ceiling, profile, topology and registry on every run, so a future slot fill, review clearance or vendor confirmation automatically changes what may be promised, proven by a test that catches a diverging freeze. Nine mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored: forcing signature verification false failed the PRIMARY; disabling the replay-billable check failed the PROPERTY; forcing a constant `CanonicalDigest` failed GOLDEN; forcing verification true failed all ten SECURITY tamper subtests; faking a ceiling-digest mismatch failed CONFORMANCE; disabling the owned-versus-observed conflict check failed the MUTATION naming `conflates overlay authority`; disabling the `Kind != EventNew` guard changed the billed total from 3,500 to 16,000 and failed the billing test; disabling the ceiling-authorization loop stopped a DEFER-disposed intent being flagged; and dropping the entitlements line from the CLI failed its output test. **One out-of-scope drift was found and recorded rather than patched:** `internal/commercial.P1AManifestDigest`, a hardcoded constant, no longer matches the live `p1a-manifest.yaml` `CanonicalDigest` -- `3df52c31...` against `91fd7749...`. That is `internal/commercial`'s own drift to repair and lies outside this lane's edit scope, so the freeze binds the Phase 1 digest to `PHASE-001`'s ceiling digest instead, documented in `doc.go`

title: Define the design-partner implementation blueprint and responsibility matrix
section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: blueprint lacks customer/HCM Next/provider owner, prerequisite, input/output artifact, due/expiry, acceptance oracle, data-processing boundary, escalation or fallback for any pilot workstream; assumed customer capability reports ready
green: versioned RACI and implementation graph covers discovery through hypercare, binds every dependency to exact evidence and stop/go gate and returns `UNKNOWN|BLOCKED` for missing or stale customer/provider inputs
refactor: instantiate the reusable blueprint per tenant; customer-specific facts never alter the platform's semantic contracts
evidence: `TestImplementationBlueprintCoversEveryPilotDependencyDeliverableOwnerAndAcceptanceGate` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus the `_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Security`, `_Conformance` and `_Mutation` tests, `TestInstantiateAgainstRealRepositoryStateReportsBlockedNamingMissingCustomerAndProviderInputs`, `TestInstantiateReturnsReadyWhenEveryInputIsCurrentlyConfirmed`, `TestInstantiateNeverMutatesTheBlueprintTemplate` and the readiness contract-shape test in `tools/planning/pilotblueprint`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./tools/planning/pilotblueprint/` PASS at 81.7%, above the floor; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The blueprint is `definitions/planning/gates/customer-001-pilot-blueprint.yaml`, following the same signing and digest conventions as `PHASE-001` and the two SELECT artifacts, with `tools/planning/cmd/pilotblueprint` as its consumer. Ten workstreams -- DISCOVERY, CONFIGURATION, DATA, IDENTITY, INTEGRATION, LEGAL_REVIEW, TESTING, TRAINING, CUTOVER and HYPERCARE -- are position-checked rather than merely set-checked, and each carries exactly one owner per party across CUSTOMER, HCM_NEXT and PROVIDER with exactly one ACCOUNTABLE, role titles and never named humans, at least one dependency bound to an evidence reference and a stop/go gate with metric, threshold and action, input and output artifacts, relative due and expiry offsets so the template stays tenant-portable, an acceptance oracle, a data-processing boundary, an escalation and a fallback. **The load-bearing behaviour is that instantiating it against today's real repository state reports BLOCKED, which is what RED demands rather than a shortcoming:** RED makes "assumed customer capability reports ready" a failure and GREEN requires `UNKNOWN|BLOCKED` for missing or stale customer inputs, and no design partner exists anywhere in this repository because `WEDGE-001` selected a problem, a Promotion/Compensation failure class, not a partner. Run live, every one of the ten workstreams reports BLOCKED with named reasons -- DISCOVERY cites `no design partner has been selected anywhere in this repository (WEDGE-001 selected a problem, not a partner)` alongside the provider's placeholder suffix, and LEGAL_REVIEW additionally cites that the pinned `SELECT-001` jurisdiction profile has no named reviewer. **Crucially the schema is not rigged to fail:** fully confirmed synthetic facts report READY, stale-but-once-confirmed facts report UNKNOWN rather than BLOCKED, and naming a partner without per-workstream confirmation is still not enough, so a permanent BLOCKED is distinguishable from a broken instantiator. Every PROVIDER-party dependency gates on `pilotprovider.SatisfiesRealProviderSelectionGate()` by value rather than on `SelectionStatus` alone, the same discipline `SELECT-002` enforces on itself, so the placeholder provider can never be mistaken for a confirmed one. **REFACTOR's contract isolation is proven rather than asserted:** `Instantiate` takes the blueprint by value and only reads it, and a test re-hashes `CanonicalDigest` and deep-compares the workstreams across three contradictory tenant-fact scenarios, while a reflection check proves `ReadinessReport` and `WorkstreamReadiness` carry no semantic-contract field such as `AcceptanceOracle`, `DataProcessingBoundary`, `Escalation` or `Fallback`, only kind, status and reasons. What a stronger enforcement would need -- a `pilotprovider`-style leak scan over a real consumer in `internal/` -- is stated plainly in `doc.go`, because no onboarding orchestrator has been built for such a scan to inspect. Ten mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored and diff-confirmed: blanking DISCOVERY's escalation failed the PRIMARY naming `workstreams[0].escalation: missing`; dropping `Workstreams` from the digest payload failed GOLDEN; forcing signature verification true failed all seven SECURITY tamper cases; repointing the provider-topology reference at a nonexistent file failed CONFORMANCE; removing the acceptance-oracle check failed only that PROPERTY subtest; removing the missing-owner-per-party check failed only that MUTATION case; neutering `worseStatus` so it never escalates failed the load-bearing instantiate test with `Overall = READY, want BLOCKED`; forcing the provider gate false failed the confirmed-facts READY test; writing into the blueprint during instantiation failed both the digest-move and deep-equality assertions across all three scenarios; and adding a forbidden `Escalation` field to `WorkstreamReadiness` failed the contract-shape test naming that exact field. **One process note, self-reported by the lane and independently verified:** it typed a `git checkout` while restoring a mutated file, against this session's standing prohibition, believing the directory was not a repository. It is. The reflog was checked afterwards and contains only commits with no checkout, every commit is intact, and the working tree's modified files are exactly the expected parked work, so nothing was reverted -- but the lane's reasoning for why it was safe was wrong, and flagging it was right

title: Prove universal per-intent storage, event, effect and correction lineage
section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: intent/proposal/workflow/transaction/event/projection/outbox/effect/observation/reconciliation/repair/correction link is missing, cross-tenant, over-disclosing or non-rebuildable while aggregate completion reports true
green: family fixtures prove complete authorized redaction-safe lineage with child/trigger causation, exact watermarks/digests and `UNKNOWN|PARTIAL` instead of false completion; correction appends without breaking historical trace
refactor: generate cases from closure witnesses and shared lineage assertions; keep domain-specific events in their owners
evidence: `TestEveryAcceptedIntentFamilyHasCompleteAuthorizedRebuildableLineage` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus `TestTodo_DATA_022_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Integration`, `_Fault`, `_Security`, `_Conformance`, `_Recovery` and `_Mutation` and per-file unit tests in the new `tools/planning/lineageconformance`; no migration and no hook in the DATA-015 package. `go test -count=1 -cover ./tools/planning/lineageconformance/` PASS at 97.2%, re-run by the orchestrator; `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go test ./tools/policy/importgraph/` PASS (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. The package lives under `tools/planning` because it consumes `closurewitness`, and imports only `internal/intent`, `internal/intent/definitions` and `internal/data/lineage`. Cases are generated, never listed: one per SLICE-016 closure witness, one per child in a definition's MODEL-016 binding and one per trigger initiator the definition allows; required links come from the definition's own fields, and a link is NOT_APPLICABLE only where the definition declares it, quoting the field. `Evaluate` treats a missing intent, proposal, workflow, transaction, event, projection, outbox, effect, observation, reconciliation, repair or correction link as UNKNOWN, and a duplicate, cross-tenant, broken-causation, digest-mismatched, watermark-less, over-disclosed, unexplained-redaction, non-rebuildable, history-rewriting, trigger-mismatched or contradicted-not-applicable record as a defect; `View` gives redaction-safe reads and `CheckAppendOnly` catches history rewritten in place. A live link counts as proven only when its producer's todo is closed and its tests exist and are cited, and `VerifyReport` recomputes every status, count, the completion flag and the digest. **Live, 0 of 19 cases are COMPLETE:** `promote_worker/v1` is PARTIAL -- INTENT from its witness, PROPOSAL through REPAIR from DATA-015's `lineage.Stages`, PROJECTION from LEDGER-013 -- with OUTBOX, RECONCILIATION and CORRECTION named UNKNOWN; its two children (`change_base_pay`, `reserve_compensation_budget`) and all three trigger paths are UNKNOWN on every link including CAUSATION; the other 13 families prove only INTENT. `_Integration` writes a real ledger event, an outbox effect caused by it, provenance, a projection rebuild and a correction in embedded PostgreSQL, and the store-backed Promotion comes out PARTIAL with RECONCILIATION its only UNKNOWN link, because no store holds a reconciliation result and none is invented. `_Recovery` shows a rebuild on a fresh connection yields an identical graph digest, in-place UPDATEs of `ledger_event` and `provenance_record` are refused, and a second correction only appends. Every defect in RED is planted in a fixture, and each check first confirms the clean fixture lacks it. Nine lane mutations failed by name. **An orchestrator mutation disabling `VerifyReport`'s aggregate-completion comparison survived the whole suite**, because every forged report also rewrote a case status and the per-case check masked it; a forgery flipping only `Complete` with a resealed digest was added to `_Mutation`, which now fails on that mutation and passes when restored. Recorded limitations: `DefaultProducers()` is hand-written -- each claim is checked against the todo registry and test names, but the attribution of DATA-015 and LEDGER-013 to definitions is the lane's reading of their docs, not a registry fact; no store holds reconciliation results, so no family can reach COMPLETE yet; child and trigger causation has no producer anywhere in the tree; the live Promotion outcome and outbox are proven by DATA-022's own Integration test but deliberately not counted as a registered producer; and the golden digest is pinned to hand-built definitions so it does not break when the real catalog changes

title: Propagate overload, retry and circuit state end to end
section: 32. Production identity, key custody and edge enforcement
red: Nested 429/503/timeouts consume one bounded logical retry budget and produce `ADMIT|QUEUE|DEFER|DEGRADE|REJECT`
green: No retry storm or duplicate effect
refactor: Keep the tested contract behind its semantic owner, remove duplication and rerun the named unit, integration, conformance, race, fuzz, security and recovery suites that apply without changing observable behavior
evidence: `TestTodo_EDGE_007` (ten subtests: each of the five outcomes is produced by its condition and the mapping is total -- an unrecognised `BackpressureAction`, `RetryDisposition` or the zero-value `CircuitState("")` all map to REJECT, never ADMIT, and an unconfigured breaker rejects with `CIRCUIT_BREAKER_UNCONFIGURED` rather than admitting or panicking; an OPEN circuit within cooldown still rejects on a later check rather than being re-probed as healthy), `_Fault` (three different failure signals -- 429, 503 and timeout -- at the same attempt number all collide on one stored receipt, `Provisioner.Snapshot` showing `Consumed == 1`, with exhaustion producing REJECT rather than another attempt), `_Race` (50 goroutines racing the identical attempt leave `Consumed == 1`; 20 goroutines with distinct attempts never exceed the configured budget), `_Security` (tenant scoping of budget and circuit state), `_Mutation` (500 nested failures against a budget of 3 perform exactly 3 effects then stay REJECT with no effect) and `FuzzTodo_EDGE_007` (564,604 execs over 30s, 66 interesting inputs, no crasher; oracle is that over arbitrary 429/503/timeout/success sequences the effects performed never exceed the budget and every outcome is one of the five) in `internal/connectivity/edge` (`overload.go`: `Coordinator.Decide`, `CircuitBreaker`/`CircuitState`, `RetryLedger`, `attemptIdentity`, the total `BackpressureAction`->`Outcome` mapping); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/connectivity/edge/` PASS at 76.7% with every pre-existing edge test unchanged and `go test -count=1 ./internal/operations/admission/` still PASS, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Composed rather than forked: this is the third todo in a row over one bounded logical retry budget, and instead of a third ledger it uses `admission.DecideBackpressure` for the health signal, `admission.Provisioner` (through a thin `RetryLedger`, mirroring EVENT-003's `outbox.RetryAccount`) as the single replay-safe budget owner, and `admission.Outcome` directly as the RED vocabulary. `internal/operations/admission` was not modified. The genuinely new logic is the total action->outcome mapping and the circuit-breaker concept, which did not exist anywhere in the repository. Reviewer fix: staticcheck U1000 flagged a leftover `combineOutcomes` helper whose most-restrictive-wins logic `Decide` already applies inline via `outcomeSeverity`; removed as duplication rather than wired in

section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD

The header and message keys are unified before hashing: if both are present and disagree the request is refused with `ErrIdempotencyKeyMismatch`, and the resolved key is hashed together with the principal/tenant/capability scope so the same logical request over HTTP and over the message path resolves to one digest. An exact replay returns the stored outcome rather than re-executing -- the distinction is observable because the effect counter stays at one -- while the same key with a changed payload returns `*PayloadConflict` without touching the effect at all, which is the clause a key-only cache would silently fail. `ExpectedRevision` is a `*uint64` so "no precondition requested" stays distinct from "expected revision zero", and a zero on either side is refused rather than treated as a match. The executor closes its ready channel in a defer, so a failing effect can never strand the waiters

title: Implement GetExecutionReceipt and ExportIntentEvidence endpoints
section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD
red: receipt/export reveals unauthorized fields/existence, omits intent→proposal→approval→transaction→observation→reconciliation lineage, uses ambient current data, creates unbounded synchronous archive, formula-injects spreadsheet output or unsigned/tampered package verifies
green: receipt returns authorized immutable summary/digest; export creates one idempotent long-running operation binding purpose/scope/fields/watermarks/redaction/format/expiry and produces encrypted signed offline-verifiable package with exact exclusions and zero source mutation

evidence: `TestEvidenceEndpointsEnforcePurposeRedactionManifestAndOperationSemantics` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Property`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Golden`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Race`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Integration`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Fault`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Security`, `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Conformance` and `TestTodo_EP_EVID_001_Mutation` in `internal/transport/evidence` (`server.go`, `receipt_handler.go`, `export_handler.go`, `crypto.go`, `lineage.go`, `types.go`, `memory.go`), composing `internal/evidence.Assemble`/`Verify`/`Redacted` (EVIDENCE-001), `internal/transport/operations.Record`/`Store` for the long-running operation, `internal/operations/export` for artifact rendering (EXPORT-001) and `internal/cryptoagility` for signing; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/transport/evidence/` PASS at 78.0%, with `./internal/transport/manifest/` 88.3%, `./internal/transport/operations/` 67.5% and `./internal/evidence/` 90.6% all still passing; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and driftgate, apigate, substratecoverage, enginecoverage, racepolicy, traceability and intentcoverage all pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The ambient-data clause is proven by a test that can actually fail. An export reads `LineageSource.Snapshot` exactly once and every downstream artifact derives from that one read; the test injects a lineage source that returns different content on every call and counts them, so an implementation that re-read its source mid-run produces a manifest disagreeing with its own artifacts and is caught. Verified failable by injecting that exact regression, which failed with `lineage source read 2 times during one export`, and passing again on revert. Package integrity is layered and real, not stubbed: `OpenAndVerify` checks the `cryptoagility` signature, then the AES-256-GCM authentication tag, then the manifest digest, then each artifact digest; the Security test flips a ciphertext byte, strips the signature and decrypts with a wrong key, and all three are rejected. Formula injection is neutralised in the human artifact and the exact bytes preserved in the machine artifact, tested with payloads beginning `=`, `+`, `-`, `@`, tab and carriage return. The six lineage hops are asserted individually -- omitting any one, and separately marking any one ABSENT, both fail the export closed -- rather than by a non-empty check. The export returns an operation reference before the archive is built, and the same request twice returns one operation, proven under 32 concurrent callers. **A genuine contract gap, reported rather than forced.** `GetExecutionReceiptResponse.execution_receipt.receipt` is wire-typed `ZeroEffectReceipt`, whose own constructor rejects a non-zero effect count and whose `ReceiptMode` admits only PREFLIGHT and SIMULATE. This todo's RED clauses describe `internal/evidence.BusinessExecutionReceipt` -- a closed, executed intent, where effects are legitimately present. Placing one inside the other would either misstate the effect count or leave the message's declared invariant unchecked, so `GetExecutionReceipt` serves only genuine zero-effect records and the full lineage-bearing receipt is carried by `ExportIntentEvidence`'s operation result, whose `CanonicalDigestReference` exists for exactly that. Closing this properly needs a proto change and is out of a lane's reach. **Boundaries.** The four ports have in-memory implementations only and `EvidenceService` is registered in no composition root, so these endpoints are contract-complete but not yet reachable in a running server; escalated. Key custody is out of scope -- the signer and package key are supplied directly, with no rotation or KMS policy. The zero-source-mutation proof counts writes to the two writable ports and relies on `LineageSource` exposing no write method; it is weaker than the SQL-parsing proof used for EP-WORK-003 and should be strengthened once real adapters exist. The Integration test reaches a real gRPC server and interceptor chain over bufconn but no database. No race detector is available on this host, so the Race entry is a 32-goroutine determinism test rather than a `-race` run

section: 60. Canonical gRPC services, grpcbridge HTTP endpoints and endpoint TDD

evidence: `TestIntentSubmitCancelSupersedeEndpointsRespectRevisionAuthorityAndIrreversibility` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Property`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Golden`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Race`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Integration`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Fault`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Security`, `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Conformance` and `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Mutation` in `internal/intent/app` (`lifecycle_endpoints.go`, `lifecycle_contract_test.go`, `lifecycle_harness_test.go`), with the same matrix names re-run over the HTTP/gRPC pair in `internal/transport/endpoint` (`intent_lifecycle_endpoints_test.go`) and the kernel contracts in `internal/intent` (`submission.go`, `cancellation.go`, `supersession.go` and their tests); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 87.4% (`internal/intent`), 82.5% (`internal/intent/lifecycle`), 79.0% (`internal/transport/endpoint`), 88.3% (`internal/transport/manifest`), 42.5% (`internal/intent/app`, raised from 22.9% and still under its recorded `below_floor` exception) and 16.0% (`internal/intent/app/pgstore`, likewise under its exception); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and driftgate, apigate, substratecoverage, enginecoverage, racepolicy, traceability and intentcoverage all pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The clause -- cancellation must never lie about whether the effect already happened -- is closed against a real obstacle: `CancelIntentResponse` carries only an `IntentInstance` and the proto has no cancellation-outcome enum, so the four GREEN answers are told entirely through the dimensional tuple. CANCELLED moves RequestState to CANCELLED with Execution NOT_PLANNED or BLOCKED; CANCELLATION_PENDING moves nothing; TOO_LATE moves nothing and leaves RequestState as it stood, because Execution is already COMMITTED and saying CANCELLED would falsify the record; REPAIR_REQUIRED moves Execution to REPAIR_REQUIRED and refuses without a repair reference. `CancelInstance` switches over every `ExecutionState` and every `CancellationPoint` by name with no permissive default, and `TestTodo_EP_INTENT_003_Integration` seeds four intents in four execution conditions and asserts the four returned tuples are pairwise distinct reading nothing but the response, so a partial mapping fails rather than passing on the common case. Supersede is proven non-mutating by a field-by-field diff rather than an existence check: the original's `protomap.InstanceToProto` encoding is captured before and after, exactly RequestState, InstanceVersion and the two transition timestamps are cleared, and `proto.Equal` must hold over everything else including a seeded prior `ProposalRevision`. The RED clause about broadened authority is closed structurally in `specForSupersede` -- tenant, organization scope, initiator and purpose all come from the authenticated principal and never from the original -- and asserted by value: the original is seeded with a VP-People delegation chain and a different initiator, and the successor is required to carry the caller's own principal id and an empty delegation chain, with a guard that fails if the fixture ever stops seeding the chain. One latent defect was fixed along the way: `Definition.LifecycleProfiles` narrowed `Transitions` but kept the full kernel state list, so any narrowed definition's profile failed its own reachability validation as soon as a `lifecycle.Machine` was built from it. CANCELLATION_PENDING is also reported but not durably recorded -- neither the proto nor `Instance` has a field for a cancellation awaiting a safe point, so nothing later honours the request; that gap is escalated rather than papered over. And `internal/intent/app/pgstore.MutateLifecycle` mirrors `BindOutcome`'s compare-and-swap but is proven only by its pre-transaction validation, not against a live PostgreSQL

title: Apply retention, holds and crypto-erasure without falsifying chronology
section: 27. Authoritative ledger implementation
red: hold permits payload destruction, erasure removes minimal event chronology/digest or redacted payload is returned as ordinary present value
green: disposition preserves minimum immutable envelope and explicit `PAYLOAD_ERASED/RESTRICTED/HELD` state; hash/integrity and hold evidence remain verifiable
refactor: payload encryption boundary is classification-driven
evidence: `TestTodo_LEDGER_011` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Golden`, `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_011`, `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Race`, `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_Mutation` and `TestTodo_LEDGER_011_PayloadStateVocabularyAgrees` in `internal/data/ledger/disposition` (`disposition.go`, `types.go`, `doc.go`), with `internal/data/ledger/reader.go` extended and migration `00285_ledger_011_payload_disposition.sql` adding the append-only `ledger_payload_disposition` table. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.0% (`internal/data/ledger/disposition`) and 70.2% (`internal/data/ledger`), with checkpoint 87.1%, commit 75.9%, evidence 86.7%, hashchain 71.9%, lineage 79.2% and temporal 90.5% unchanged, `./migrations/` PASS at 81.5%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The clause -- an erasure must not be able to lie in either direction -- is closed at the **default** read path, not an opt-in one. `EventRecord` gains a `PayloadState` with no permissive zero value, and `ReadStream`/`ReadEvent` LEFT JOIN the disposition table and unconditionally withhold the payload whenever a disposition row names the event, so the ten pre-existing callers in `internal/data/projection/critical`, `internal/data/projection`, `internal/data/provenance`, `internal/data/queryplans`, `internal/data/rebuild` and `internal/intent/app/pgstore` inherit the withholding without change. `TestTodo_LEDGER_011` reads back through plain `ledger.NewReader().ReadEvent` rather than through `disposition.ReadView` precisely so that an opt-in-only withholding would fail, and it distinguishes an erased payload from an event that never carried one by asserting the two states differ and neither is empty. Chronology is proven preserved by name: `assertSameEventColumns` compares all twenty `ledger_event` columns before and after and fails naming the exact column that changed, and `hashchain.Digester.Verify` is called against real PostgreSQL before and after with an identical head asserted. The hold clause has no check-then-act gap -- `Erase` composes `recordsmeta.DisposeCopy`, which locks `record_copy_link` FOR UPDATE and evaluates `hold_state` under that same lock -- and a refused attempt is asserted to leave the hold status, its ACTIVE intersection and the event row untouched. `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_011` ran ~368K executions with zero crashers over payload bytes and arbitrary classification strings, asserting that exactly the two declared classifications succeed and map to `PAYLOAD_ERASED`/`RESTRICTED` while near-misses such as `"standard"` or a trailing space are refused rather than defaulted, and that a chain built from fuzzed bytes verifies field-for-field before and after. **Boundaries, stated rather than implied.** Crypto-erasure is **modelled, not real**: this codebase's append path never encrypts an inline payload, so there is no key protecting bytes already on disk and `Erase` records a symbolic key reference as governance evidence of a decision, not proof of cryptographic unrecoverability. `ledger_event.payload` is never physically zeroed for either mechanism, which is not achievable without abandoning that table's append-only trigger and grants; both mechanisms' real guarantee is that the read layer never returns the bytes again. The fuzz target is pure and in-memory, following the existing `FuzzTodo_LEDGER_012` precedent, so the database-backed guarantees are carried by the PRIMARY, Race and Mutation tests instead. `TestTodo_DB_020_Golden` in `internal/data/queryplans` was regenerated because the new LEFT JOIN turns `LEDGER_STREAM_REPLAY` into a nested loop over two indexed scans with no sequential scan introduced; it failed once under four concurrent embedded-PostgreSQL instances and then passed three consecutive full-package runs, so it is recorded here as planner variance under load rather than a stale golden

Read as a pure sizing model rather than a load test, which is what RED's "persist zero authoritative rows, business events, outbox entries, human work and provider requests" clause requires: the 100k+ timer drain is a dimension the model bounds (`MinTimerBacklogCapacity`), not an action any test performs, so nothing here starts PostgreSQL or generates load. Storage covers rows, index bytes, WAL bytes, locks, connection pool and vacuum seconds; timers cover backlog, drain rate and drain budget; artifacts cover named object classes each with throughput and memory. Every dimension is a `Dimension{Capacity, Measured}` whose zero value or empty unit is rejected as `MISSING_OR_INVALID` rather than read as within budget, and `ratio` additionally guards a non-positive limit so headroom can never divide by zero. Headroom, a rollover point at 80% of capacity and the hard limit are derived per dimension, and a model missing any dimension is rejected outright with no partial completion

title: Resolve promotion eligibility consistently across the seeded workforce
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: Journeys sends users to a directory where every initially visible worker reports `No available workflows`, the sole eligible Jane record can be found only by knowing her name, or the legacy `W-1001` corpus record and the 64 seeded workers follow different promotion-eligibility rules
green: the authorized directory can filter directly to promotion-eligible workers, every displayed availability state has a server-provided reason, local-dev fixtures use one worker identity and job-architecture model, and at least four role-diverse workers exercise eligible, ineligible, active-conflict and withheld outcomes without enumeration leakage
refactor: eligibility is one server-owned projection consumed by People, Person, global actions and Journeys; no client-side role-code allowlist
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux001_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_WorkerCreationReservationIsAtomicWithItsWorker` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux001_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/browser/promoux001_people_eligibility.spec.mjs`; new `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_availability.go` and `internal/data/demoworkforce/promotion_paths.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 84.8% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`), 53.5% (`internal/data/demoworkforce`), 43.2% (`internal/intent/app`) and 68.0% (`internal/data/workeridstore`) -- the last three sit under recorded `below_floor` exceptions that this change raised rather than created; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires.** The dev stack was rebuilt (schema 285, `demo-people` seeded), and the People directory at `http://127.0.0.1:8080/workspace/app/people` was driven in a real browser: 65 people across Finance, Marketing, Legal & Compliance and Care Coordination, a `Promotion-eligible only` checkbox in the filter form, 30 of 50 visible rows offering a Workflows menu, and the remaining 20 carrying the server-provided reason `No eligible promotion role is published for this employee. Ask your HR administrator to review the job ladder and pay band.` The bare `No available workflows` string that RED names is gone from the live surface. `?eligible=1` narrows the directory to 38 rows, every one of them offering a workflow and none carrying an unavailable reason. The root cause RED describes was a job-architecture catalog gap rather than a business-rule refusal: `workforceOptions()` published promotion paths only from the fixed four-worker corpus, whose job codes do not overlap the 60 demoworkforce codes, so every seeded worker resolved zero choices for a structural reason indistinguishable from ineligibility. `demoworkforce.PromotionPaths()` now publishes the demo company's own computed ladder into the same `WorkforceOptions` contract. Enumeration leakage is closed in both directions. `ResolvePromotionAvailability(authorized, hasPath, activeConflict)` checks authorization first and exhaustively, with no permissive default, so every worker collapses to one `PromotionWithheld` code for an unauthorized viewer; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` drives three different underlying states through an unauthorized viewer and requires exactly one distinct reason string, then requires ineligible and active-conflict to differ for an authorized one. A zero-value trap was closed during review: `personPromotionEligible` treated an unset `PromotionAvailability` as eligible, and the regression test asserted that an unevaluated worker received a launchable action and no reason at all -- a Person built by any future page, provider or partial projection would have offered a promotion the server never authorized. The gate now requires an explicit `PromotionEligible`, the shared fixtures say so, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Regression` pins both halves; restoring the permissive gate fails it with `a worker with no server verdict was offered a launchable promotion`. Two independent defects were fixed alongside. `demo-people` could not seed at all because `ingestDemoPhotos` demanded bit-identical regeneration of proxies whose checked-in bytes had drifted for `hc-042`/`hc-055`; it now trusts an already-published tracked proxy, and no tracked asset bytes were modified. And `workeridstore.Store.Reserve` self-committed while `journeyEngine.CreateWorker` inserted the worker row in a separate later transaction, so any failure between the two permanently orphaned a worker number in an append-only reservation table; `ReserveTx` now threads the caller's transaction through both steps. **Boundaries.** The Playwright spec was written but not executed here; the live evidence above is a real browser driven against the real server, not that spec. `TestTodo_SVC_013_Integration` in `cmd/migrate` fails on migration rollback, which is pre-existing -- 00284 raises the same irreversible exception and predates this work

title: Prevent overlapping active promotions and route users to the existing journey
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: a worker with a nonterminal promotion still exposes `Start Promotion`, or concurrent starts create more than one active promotion before execution-time conflict checking
green: a tenant-scoped active-intent guard admits exactly one promotion per worker and overlapping effective window; replays resolve to the same intent; People and Person replace Start with `Open active promotion`; a conflicting actor sees a safe explanation and zero new proposal, work item or domain mutation
refactor: the guard belongs to promotion admission and is projected to clients; UI suppression is not the integrity boundary
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Recovery` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`guard_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` in `internal/data/promotionguard` (`race_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` in `test/bootstrap` (`promoux002_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux002_test.go`); new `migrations/00286_promoux002_active_promotion_guard.sql`, `internal/data/promotionguard` and `internal/intent/app/promotionguard_wire.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.6% (`internal/data/promotionguard`), 81.1% (`internal/transport/journey`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 81.7% (`internal/data/schema`), 81.5% (`migrations`) and 53.8% (`cmd/migrate`), with `internal/humanwork/workspace` and `internal/intent/app` raised under their recorded `below_floor` exceptions rather than newly violating them; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. REFACTOR's clause -- the guard belongs to promotion admission and UI suppression is not the integrity boundary -- is what this todo turns on, so the guarantee is a database constraint rather than an application check. `promotion_active_intent_guard` carries a partial unique index on `(tenant_id, worker_ref, effective_date) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'`, and `promotionguard.Admit` is a single `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING` -- never a SELECT that precedes the write. Two concurrent transactions may both read no conflict; only one can commit, because PostgreSQL evaluates the index as part of each INSERT's own commit. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Race` proves it with 12 goroutines on genuinely independent connections and transactions released from a common barrier, each presenting a distinct idempotency key so the test measures exclusion between different requests rather than deduplication of one retry, and asserts exactly one admission plus a durable row count rather than merely the absence of an error. The zero-mutation clause is proven by counting rather than by asserting success, twice over: a `countingExecutor`/`countingBeginner` wrapping the real `dbport.Tx` (the pattern `internal/humanwork/workitem/decide_approval_test.go` established) requires every mutating statement a refused start issues to target `promotion_active_intent_guard` and nothing else, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` additionally diffs row counts across `intent_instance`, `ledger_event`, `work_item` and the domain tables. The guard is proven to hold with the UI entirely out of the picture: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_002_Security` calls `journeyEngine.Propose` directly with no HTTP, gRPC or page involved, and the PRIMARY calls `Admit` directly. Four pre-existing tests were updated rather than weakened, each of which had assumed two proposals for one worker's single effective date are both admitted -- the exact defect this todo closes. `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Integration`'s digest subtest now asserts the second request is refused with `journey.propose_promotion.active_conflict`, keeps its original content-digest claim by computing `app.PromotionProposeRequestDigest` on the refused request directly, and adds a row count proving no second intent was created; `TestTodo_PROMO_007_Mutation`, `TestTodo_WF_RUN_027_Bootstrap_Security` and `TestJourneyDecideRejectReachesTheRejectedTerminal` now use distinct, non-overlapping effective dates so their own zero-effect and terminal claims still exercise two genuinely admitted proposals. **Boundary, and it is a real one.** `promotionguard.Release` is implemented and unit-tested but is called from no production code, because no write-time hook fires when an intent reaches a terminal stage (`deriveJourneyStage` is read-time only, computed from workflow runtime nodes). A guard row is therefore created ACTIVE and never closed, so once a promotion is rejected or completed, re-proposing for that same worker and effective date is refused permanently; the workaround is a different effective date. This also disagrees with the UI, whose `activeConflict` signal still comes from the pre-existing `ListJourneys` non-terminal scan rather than the guard table, so after a journey goes terminal the UI offers Start while the server refuses it. RED frames the guard around a worker with a _nonterminal_ promotion, so blocking past terminal is outside the contract this todo was built for; escalated separately rather than left implied. Two registry rows were added during review that the lane could not write itself: `promotion_active_intent_guard`, and `ledger_payload_disposition`, which LEDGER-011 shipped without a `definitions/storage/storage-disposition.yaml` entry and which had left `TestTodo_DATA_001` red since that merge

title: Enforce and explain separation of duties across promotion approvals
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: one principal completes both finance and manager approval for the same proposal, the work items share an undifferentiated `principal:promotion-approver` owner, or the UI offers an approval without naming the authority and conflict that permit it
green: approver resolution binds each requirement to its authority class and separation constraints; the same principal is refused where duties conflict; reassignment preserves the proposal digest; and the UI states `Waiting for <role>`, assigned person or protected-group label, due date, the viewer's acting authority and why the action is or is not available
refactor: separation is evaluated by the approval owner before claim or completion; presentation consumes the resulting disposition
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Security`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Race` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Mutation` in `internal/workflow/steps/approval` (`promoux003_test.go`, `promoux003_race_test.go`, `promoux003_mutation_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Integration` in `internal/humanwork/workitem` (`promoux003_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux003_test.go`); new `internal/humanwork/approverclass`, `internal/humanwork/workitem/separation.go`, `internal/humanwork/workitem/disposition.go`, `internal/workflow/steps/approval/authority_recheck.go` and `internal/humanwork/productui/approval_disposition.go`; no migration required, because the guarantee is row locking over the existing `work_item` table rather than a new one. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 75.2% (`internal/workflow/steps/approval`), 75.6% (`internal/humanwork/workitem`), 100.0% (`internal/humanwork/approverclass`), 94.4% (`internal/workflow/promotionexec`), 76.1% (`internal/platform/execution`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 43.5% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised, not lowered); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The concurrent double-approval is made impossible by the database rather than by a check that precedes the write. `Store.LockApprovalSiblings` issues `SELECT ... WHERE tenant_id AND proposal_ref AND kind='APPROVAL' ORDER BY work_item_id FOR UPDATE` inside the caller's own transaction; ordering by `work_item_id` means every caller acquires the same locks in the same order, so two racing completions cannot deadlock, and because both requirements on one proposal name the _same_ row set only one transaction can hold them. `approval.Complete` takes that lock before it reads any state and before the completing write, and holds it for the rest of the call, so the loser blocks until the winner commits and then observes the committed conflict and refuses with `ErrSeparationConflict`. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Race` proves it with two real PostgreSQL connections and transactions released from a barrier, stable across five runs. RED's undifferentiated-owner clause is closed structurally rather than by convention: the new `approverclass` package derives provably distinct finance and manager principals from one base, and both `internal/platform/execution` and `internal/intent/app` route each requirement to its derived owner instead of the shared `principal:promotion-approver` the dev environment had been minting for both. Digest preservation under reassignment is proven by diff rather than by a non-empty check: the Integration test captures the full durable record, forces a real reassignment through the HRBP departure fallback, then requires `ProposalRef` equality plus field-by-field equality of tenant, item id, kind, work type, correlation, instance, node, requirement ref, policy route, visibility, org scope, deadline, created-at and subjects -- while asserting the owner actually moved, so the equality claim cannot pass vacuously. REFACTOR's clause that separation is evaluated by the approval owner rather than by whichever surface calls it is proven with the UI entirely absent: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_003_Security` drives a conflicted principal through `workitem.Store.DecideApproval` composed with the new `SeparationAuthority` driver -- no HTTP, no journey engine, no page -- and every PRIMARY and RACE subtest calls `approval.Complete` directly. `SeparationAuthority` fills the concrete `workitem.AuthorityRecheckPort` seam that EP-WORK-003 left unimplemented and whose absence was recorded as a boundary when that todo closed. Presentation consumes the disposition rather than recomputing it. `ApprovalDispositionProjectionFrom` is a pure field copy and `approvalDispositionCardProps` only localizes; no membership, authority or conflict logic exists in `productui`. The rendered card states the five facts GREEN names, and both the props and the rendered markup are asserted not to leak -- a candidate-set owner renders as a generic protected-group phrase with `candidates:` and `sha256:` required absent from the emitted HTML, and a conflicted viewer's refusal names no second principal. **Boundaries.** The disposition card was not observed on screen: the dev corpus holds no approval work items, so `/workspace/app/work` renders `0 items`, and the card is proven instead by asserting the real rendered HTML through `ui.RenderToString` on the same server-rendered path this page uses. The assigned-person label humanizes a raw principal reference because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`; a real display name is a larger, separate feature. `SeparationAuthority` protects the domain capability rather than a live endpoint, because EP-WORK-003's transport still has no production completion wiring -- a pre-existing gap already escalated, neither created nor worsened here -- and `execute.Driver.CompleteApproval` inherits the guarantee but has no production caller. Separately, `TestTodo_DB_EDGE_003_IntegrationPromotionCompositionRetriesSerializableAndRechecksApproval` had a hardcoded 20s budget that turned machine load into a false failure; confirmed pre-existing by running it in a worktree of unmodified HEAD, where it failed identically at 22.9s and 32.4s, and raised to 120s with every assertion unchanged

title: Replace free-text target positions with authorized vacancy selection and reservation evidence
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: an arbitrary guessed identifier such as `POS-ENG-MGR-101` is accepted without proving existence, vacancy, compatibility, effective-date capacity and reservation ownership
green: an accessible server-filtered picker shows only authorized compatible positions with title, organization, manager, location, vacancy window and reservation state; selection binds the immutable position revision; simulation explains advisory versus durable capacity; stale or concurrently reserved choices fail before approval with a recoverable alternative-selection state
refactor: the browser carries only the selected position revision reference; validation and reservation remain owned by Position
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Security` in `internal/domains/promotion` (`promoux004_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Race` in `internal/data/positionguard` (`guard_test.go`, `race_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Browser` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_Accessibility` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux004_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_WorkspaceLivePath` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux004_test.go`); new `migrations/00287_promoux004_position_slot_guard.sql`, `internal/domains/position/revisionref.go`, `internal/domains/promotion/target_position.go`, `internal/domains/promotion/positionpicker`, `internal/data/positionguard`, `internal/data/positionfacts` and `internal/humanwork/productui/position_picker.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 71.2% (`internal/domains/position`), 77.1% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 77.5% (`positionpicker`), 79.0% (`internal/data/positionguard`), 70.5% (`internal/data/positionfacts`), 98.6% (`internal/intent/definitions`), 72.1% (`internal/workflow/simulate`), 81.5% (`migrations`), 93.2% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 45.9% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. RED named a guessed identifier being accepted, so the decisive proof is that one is refused on the path a user actually reaches rather than in the evaluator alone. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_004_WorkspaceLivePath` composes a `Cell` the way a live deployment does, with a pgtest-backed `ExecutionDB` and tenant mapping, and drives `Cell.WorkspacePort().ReadPromotion`: a guessed `POS-ENG-MGR-101` comes back `StatusBlocked` with `CodeTargetPositionNotFound` and `Simulation.Executable == false`, the same refusal holds for an independently composed cell and tenant, and a request naming no position at all still reaches `StatusReady`. The check is no longer opt-in: any non-empty `TargetPlacement.PositionID` is decoded as a `position.RevisionRef` and evaluated, so a value that does not decode is refused on the existence ground. Each of the five grounds has its own subtest constructing a scenario where only that ground fails -- existence, compatibility, vacancy, effective-date revision currency and reservation ownership -- rather than a single invalid-position assertion that could pass with four of five wired. A bare identifier proves the first four; the fifth is a write and requires the richer `PositionSelection`, which is GREEN's advisory-versus-durable distinction. The reservation race is settled by the database: `promotion_target_position_guard_one_active_window`, a partial unique index on `(tenant_id, position_ref, effective_date) WHERE status = 'ACTIVE'` that PostgreSQL evaluates as part of each `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... RETURNING`'s own commit rather than by a read preceding the write, proven with 12 concurrent goroutines on independent connections. Enumeration is closed by passing the identical `position.Authorizer` to both the picker and the evaluator and requiring a guessed unauthorized position's `Finding` to be byte-for-byte identical to a genuinely nonexistent one's, so the refusal itself cannot be used to discover which position ids are real. Three real defects were found and fixed along the way. Ground four had used `CompareInStream`, which errors with `ErrRevisionNotOrdered` on the opaque revisions the real adapter mints; it now uses `Equal`, which is the exact binding REFACTOR asks for. Building the production `internal/data/positionfacts` adapter against real PostgreSQL surfaced a timezone bug -- date extraction did not normalize to UTC first, so a server in `America/New_York` shifted every date by up to a day -- and an off-by-one translating DB-009's exclusive `effective_to` boundary into the domain's inclusive end-date convention. One deliberate contract change: `target_position_ref` moved from `Required: true` to `Required: false` in `internal/intent/definitions`. The kernel had been stricter than the domain while proving less -- `checkPlacement` blocks on a missing target job code and grade but has never required a position, so the presence check only guaranteed a non-empty string and a guessed one satisfied it. A named position is now proven against the real Position domain, which is a stronger guarantee than presence ever gave, and job and grade remain blocking so the shape is not unconstrained. **Boundaries.** Ground five is never exercised on the live `journeyEngine.Propose` path: only the read-only preview reaches a wired `PositionReader`, and no caller yet supplies the `ProposalRef`/`IdempotencyKey`/`Reservations` a durable reservation needs, which would require real position rows seeded into the dev corpus and the commit path wired. `positionpicker` filters a caller-supplied candidate set because `position.PositionFacts` exposes no listing port; a real directory source is a separate feature. `TestTodo_MSRC_006_Golden` in `internal/intent/model/deferred` fails on a drifted DB-016 preview digest, confirmed unrelated here -- `go list -deps` shows `tools/gen/deferredschema` depends on none of the changed packages and generates its own content rather than reading the storage registry -- and escalated separately
