Cycle safety is real reachability rather than a single-hop guard. `org.DetectManagerCycle` walks the proposed manager's actual ancestor chain through `ResolveManagerRelationships` and asks whether the promoted worker appears in it, so a cycle that closes two or more hops up is caught; `TestDetectManagerCycle_MultiHop` and the PRIMARY's multi-hop subtest both build A reports to B reports to C and refuse promoting A to manage C, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_005_Integration` reproduces that same shape against real PostgreSQL rows. The converse is proven too, because a check that refused every deep chain would pass a cycle test while breaking the product: `TestDetectManagerCycle_DeepChainAdmitted`, the PRIMARY's legitimate-deep-chain subtest and the Integration test's fourth worker all admit a four-hop chain that closes no cycle. The detector reports three outcomes rather than a boolean that would have to guess. A chain it cannot certify -- depth exceeded, a pre-existing loop above the proposed manager, a withheld disclosure, or a stale, disagreeing or ambiguous resolution -- returns UNDETERMINED, and promotion treats that as blocking with its own finding: `CycleSafe` requires both no cycle and no undetermined result, so an unresolved chain is never reported safe by omission. The materiality clause is proven to re-run the same checks rather than a cheaper subset: the PRIMARY runs `PreflightPromotion` twice changing only the affected-report scope, requires the inputs and result digests to move and the new run to find the cycle, and additionally requires **every pre-existing unrelated finding from the first run to reappear verbatim** -- so a re-validation that quietly dropped checks would fail. REFACTOR holds: the traversal lives in `internal/domains/org` and promotion composes its typed `ManagementImpact` effect rather than copying graph logic, with `internal/data/orgfacts` supplying the first production `org.WorkerFacts` adapter in the tree, reading `journey_worker`'s `manager_relationship_ref`. **A pre-existing defect was found and escalated rather than silently inherited.** Three commit-path cycle checks -- `org.ManagerMutation` at `manager_mutation.go:58`, `promotion/commit.Command` at `command.go:147` and `promotion/localcommit` at `localcommit.go:335` -- test membership in an ancestor list that nothing ever populates with a real resolution, so their self-reference half works while their multi-hop half always passes. They are dormant because P1A simulates `promote_worker` and never executes it, but they become silent no-ops the moment execution is enabled, which is why the Mutation test feeds a correctly computed list directly rather than pretending that path is wired. **Boundaries.** The HTTP form does not yet collect a target-manager selection, so the capability is composed end to end -- `Cell` to `orgfacts.Reader` to `PreflightRequest` -- but reachable only through the Go API today, the same shape PROMOUX-004 left for its durable reservation. The review card shows the manager as a raw worker id because no directory lookup is reachable from `productui`, the boundary PROMOUX-003 recorded. The full `test/bootstrap` and root suites were not run, per AGENTS.md's multi-hour guidance; every golden that actually broke was regenerated through its own package's `-update` flag

title: Show the authorized compensation baseline and exact entry guardrail before submit
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: the promotion form shows current base as `—` while enforcing a hidden percentage rule, or expresses only `0.0500..0.1800` after rejection
green: after target-role selection, authorized purpose-bound data displays current exact Money, permitted increase percent, exact minimum and maximum annual Money, band position, currency and effective-date basis; the input constrains and explains the range without floating-point arithmetic; unauthorized viewers receive a typed unavailable action rather than inferred pay
refactor: formatting uses shared Money and Percentage value types and locale services; the client never recomputes the authoritative guardrail
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) in `internal/domains/promotion` (`compensation_guardrail_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Security` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_I18N` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`compensation_guardrail_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Integration` in `internal/data/workforce` (`compensation_guardrail_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest); new `internal/domains/promotion/compensation_guardrail.go` and `internal/humanwork/productui/compensation_guardrail.go`; no migration and no new storage row required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 78.4% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 93.2% (`internal/humanwork/productui`) and 81.7% (`internal/data/workforce`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. RED named a form expressing its guardrail as the raw range `0.0500..0.1800`, so the no-floating-point clause is proven by a test that would actually catch a float rather than by inspection. All money and percentage arithmetic lives in `permittedIncreasePercent`, using `Money.Sub` and `Decimal.Div` at a declared six-digit scale with `values.RoundingHalfEven` and no `float64` on the path; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006/NoFloatDrift` picks 1000000.03 and 1180000.09 -- the textbook double-precision trap scaled to salary figures -- and **first proves the trap is real on this platform**, failing with an explicit instruction to choose different cents if a float64 subtraction of those literals ever does reproduce 180000.06, before asserting the guardrail returns exactly 180000.06 and 0.180000. That self-validating shape means the test cannot silently decay into a vacuous assertion. The client is proven not to recompute the authoritative guardrail adversarially rather than agreeably: the Browser test supplies a projection whose maximum and permitted percent are deliberately not what `base * 1.18` or `(max - current) / current` would produce, and requires the rendered HTML to carry the supplied projection's exact strings rather than the recomputation. A well-formed fixture would have agreed either way and hidden a client-side calculation. The inference channel is closed in both layers, because a permitted range discloses the baseline -- a maximum of base times 1.18 lets a reader solve for base. At the domain, all six non-VALUE presence states (absent, null, unknown, redacted, unavailable, not-applicable) leave every data field zero and produce byte-identical `Canonical()` encodings, so the cause itself is not a signal. At the presentation, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_Security` strips HTML tags -- so an `<h3>` cannot be mistaken for a leaked digit -- and requires zero digits, no percent sign and none of the authorized render's exact strings for both NOT_AUTHORIZED and BAND_UNRESOLVED, with an authorized control render proving the check is not vacuous. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_006_I18N` distinguishes locales rather than rendering three and asserting one string: en-US emits `550,000.00` where de-DE emits `550.000,00`, with grouping and decimal separators genuinely swapped for both money and percent, `USD` present in all three, and `ar` asserted RTL with Arabic-script text distinct from the English and German titles. **Boundaries.** No adapter in this tree implements `rewards.CompensationFacts` or `rewards.PayBandCatalog` against real PostgreSQL -- every production composition, including PROMOUX-004's and 005's, wires both from `internal/domains/fixtures` -- so the Integration test reaches real PostgreSQL for the part that has a real adapter, a worker's stored base pay, currency and pay basis through `workforce.Store` under row-level security, and composes that with an in-memory pay-band catalog. `internal/experience/localize` only swaps separators for `de` and `fr` prefixes, so Arabic numerals follow the en-US separator convention rather than Arabic-Indic digits; that is pre-existing and shared by every component using these value types. And the card is not rendered on any page a user reaches, the third such component after PROMOUX-003's approval disposition and PROMOUX-005's promotion review; all three are escalated together rather than left as three separate footnotes

title: Present promotion validation as field-linked recoverable guidance
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: a rejected pay value produces a page-level message containing field keys, decimal fractions, Go error names or correlation internals, does not associate the error with Proposed base pay, or leaves the user at an unrelated scroll position
green: typed refusal reasons map to localized field messages with exact corrective bounds; the summary links to each invalid field; focus and scroll move predictably without losing entered values; changing a field clears only its stale error; a copyable support reference is available through diagnostics without implementation text in ordinary copy
refactor: one refusal-to-presentation mapper serves SSR and enhanced clients; do not parse human error strings
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Golden`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_I18N` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Security` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux007_test.go`); new `internal/humanwork/productui/promotion_validation.go`; `i18n.go` gained 37 `promotion_validation.*` keys per locale across en-US, de-DE and ar; no migration and no new storage row required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test was modified. REFACTOR's two clauses are both structural rather than asserted. `MapPromotionRefusal` is the single refusal-to-presentation function, and it serves both render paths because SSR calls `ui.RenderToString(Build(view))` while the enhanced client calls `ui.Render(Build(view), selector)` -- the identical Go tree compiled twice, once native and once for js/wasm, so there is no second implementation that could drift. And it never parses human error strings: the mapper keys exclusively on `Finding.Code` and does not read `Finding.Message` anywhere, which matters because that is the field the domain itself documents as carrying raw decimal fractions, denial reasons and Go error text. Verified by inspection -- the only occurrences of `.Message` in the file are comments explaining why it is never read. The stale-error clause is proven with two invalid fields rather than one, because a single-field test cannot distinguish clearing one error from clearing all of them: the PRIMARY seeds `proposed.base` and `effective_date` as invalid, clears the first, and requires the second's issue to be unchanged in message, code, field and severity with exactly one issue remaining. The leak clause is proven in both directions, since asserting only that ordinary copy is clean could be satisfied by deleting the support reference entirely. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_Security` renders a `Finding.Message` deliberately stuffed with a decimal fraction, a Go error string and a fake correlation id, strips tags, and requires none of it in visible copy -- while separately requiring the collapsed diagnostics panel to carry the exact `PreflightResult.ResultDigest`, an opaque hash the domain already computes, so support still has something to act on. Mapping is exhaustive and fails closed: all 32 `promotion.Finding` codes that exist today have explicit cases, a table-driven subtest asserts none of them reaches the fallback, and a separate subtest feeds an unrecognised code carrying an adversarial message and requires the output to be only the generic fallback text -- containing neither the code nor the leaked Go error text, decimal fraction or correlation string. Corrective bounds are quoted from PROMOUX-006's guardrail rather than recomputed: `CodeBelowBandMinimum` and `CodeAboveBandMaximum` render `MinimumAnnualized` and `MaximumAnnualized` through the shared money helper with no arithmetic in this layer, and an unavailable guardrail falls back to a bound-free message proven digit-free. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_007_I18N` distinguishes locales rather than rendering three and asserting one string: the quoted bound's grouping and decimal separators swap between en-US `500,000.00` and de-DE `500.000,00`, the surrounding sentence itself differs, and the Arabic render carries real Arabic-script characters distinct from both. **Boundary.** The mapper and its components are not wired into any page a user reaches, because no live promotion-proposal form exists yet in `internal/transport/journey` or `tools/uxqual/render/journey`. This is the fourth such component after PROMOUX-003's approval disposition, PROMOUX-005's promotion review and PROMOUX-006's compensation guardrail; all four are covered by the single escalation raised at PROMOUX-006 rather than recorded as separate footnotes. It was deliberately built to the shape those precedents established -- a server-resolved verdict with a presentation-only projection -- so the wiring is additive rather than a rewrite. The wasm hydration path is proven structurally identical rather than executed, since no browser was used here

title: Put promotion machinery behind an authorized diagnostics disclosure
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: ordinary promotion review exposes entity refs, material or plan digests, raw `SET` operations, workflow node names, work-item UUIDs, raw event codes, principals or `JourneyService` labels by default
green: the default page shows employee, proposed business changes, approvals, policy explanations, effective date, next owner and human-readable history; an authorized Technical details disclosure contains identifiers, evidence and trace references with copy controls and redaction; unauthorized viewers cannot infer hidden internals from presence, count or layout
refactor: business timeline events and diagnostic evidence are two projections over the same immutable records, not duplicated stored summaries
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Golden` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Accessibility` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux008_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Security` in `internal/transport/journey` (`promoux008_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_Browser` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_008_I18N` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux008_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 97.0% (`internal/experience/roleaccess`), 80.9% (`internal/transport/journey`), 96.6% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 87.1% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`) and 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. RED reproduced on two independent surfaces before the change. The `Technical details` disclosure in `tools/uxqual/render/journey/components.go` was rendered at two sites, both gated on nothing but `htmlIf(j.WorkerRef != "" || j.InstanceID != "", ...)` -- data presence, with no role, capability or purpose check anywhere in the path -- so every viewer who could see a journey card received `eref:v1:harborcare-demo:worker:0e30e81f-984f-5611-8570-f8c903470020` and an instance UUID, and GREEN asks for an _authorized_ disclosure. That same predicate was also the inference channel GREEN's third clause forbids, because the summary's presence was a direct function of whether internals existed; gating only the contents would have left it open. Separately `/workspace/app/work` rendered a raw work-item UUID (`01a09a09-074d-7b2d-9dc9-409e252ec222`) in its default view on a page carrying zero `<details>` elements at all, which is the RED's "work-item UUIDs" clause verbatim. Diagnostics authority is now a first-class page id, `journey-diagnostics`, carried as the same wire string through `roleaccess.PageJourneyDiagnostics`, `productui.PageJourneyDiagnostics` and `journeyclient.diagnosticsPageID`, granted to `hcm_admin`/`comp_admin` through their existing blanket grant and to `promotion_operator` explicitly, and to nobody else -- managers and HR partners who can approve a promotion still cannot read its machinery. The server gate (`internal/transport/journey/diagnostics_access.go`) fails **closed**: a nil RoleAccess store, an empty permission table and an absent explicit grant all deny, deliberately unlike the pre-existing `requirePageAction`'s permissive rolling-upgrade default, because this authority never existed before and a permissive default would have silently granted it to everyone. Identifiers are withheld from the **payload**, not merely from the view: `convert.go`'s `toJourney`, `toInstance`, `toDetail` and `toWorkItem` drop `MaterialDigest`, `CorrelationId`, `InstanceId`/`InstanceVersion`, the whole `Instance` message, `PlannedWrites`, `Ledger`, `EvidenceIds`, `Nodes`, `Transitions` and every `WorkItem.WorkItemId` for an unauthorized caller across `ListJourneys`, `ProposeJourney`, `InspectJourney`, `ExecuteJourney`, `DecideJourney` and `WatchJourney`. `WorkerRef` and `IntentID` are deliberately kept for every viewer because they are the routing keys the person-profile link and the journey's own address need, and the live check confirms that is all they are used for. The presence channel is closed by a server-derived `JourneyCard.DiagnosticsAuthorized` computed once via `cfg.CanPageAction("journey-diagnostics", "view")`, never from data presence; the detail page's `workflowSection`, `outcomeSection` and `evidenceSection`, which had rendered unconditionally whenever they held content, are gated the same way -- a defect the first evidence pass missed because it scanned only the list page. **Live matrix.** Signed in as the `admin` persona and again as a `promotion_operator`-only credential, `/workspace/app/journeys` renders 9 `Technical details` disclosures whose contents are redacted to `Worker ••••0020` and `Instance ••••9d08` with zero full UUIDs visible and two copy controls carrying the distinct accessible names `Copy Worker value` and `Copy Instance value`, the buttons writing the unredacted value through `navigator.clipboard.writeText`. Signed in as the `hiring-manager` persona (`hiring_manager`, `manager`, `intent_author`), the same page renders **0** disclosures, 0 UUIDs and 0 `eref:` occurrences in visible text, and every UUID remaining anywhere in the markup is a `href="#/journeys/<id>"` routing address -- a scan for a UUID outside an `href` attribute returned none. `/workspace/app/work` likewise fell from one raw UUID in visible text to zero for that persona. Because unauthorized viewers receive `detailsCount: 0` uniformly, there is no per-journey variation left to infer from. The `promotion_operator`-only run also answered the lane's one open question: `RoleAccess.Bootstrap`'s idempotent upsert does seed the new page id into an already-bootstrapped tenant on restart, so the grant is live without a manual migration. All six tests were mutation-verified -- ignoring `authorized` in `technicalDetailsSection` failed the PRIMARY on three subtests and diverged the GOLDEN's pinned bytes, stripping the per-row `aria-label` failed the ACCESSIBILITY, forcing the authorization check to `return true` failed every identifier assertion in the SECURITY, the same renderer mutation failed the BROWSER, and deleting the `ar` translation failed the I18N script check; each was restored and reverified green

title: Canonicalize and deduplicate promotion simulation findings
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: one budget observation appears twice with swapped internal code and message, or ordering and identity change across reloads
green: findings have a stable semantic identity, owner, severity, affected field/effect and one canonical explanation; exact duplicates collapse while independently sourced corroboration remains attributable; deterministic ordering and count survive persistence and reload
refactor: deduplication operates on typed finding identity before presentation, never on rendered strings
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Property`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Golden`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Mutation` in `internal/domains/promotion/simcontract` (`promoux009_test.go`), plus `TestTodo_PROMOUX_009_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux009_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 75.1% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 79.0% (`internal/domains/promotion/simcontract`) and 87.1% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. This todo could not be reproduced in a browser: findings are produced by a simulation and every live journey sits past that stage, so nothing was on screen to inspect and producing one would have meant proposing a promotion that mutates tenant state. The defect was therefore established from the contract and proved by driving the real rule engine in test. `promotion.Finding` (`preflight.go:134`) carried only `Code`, `Severity`, `Field` and `Message` -- no owner at all, though GREEN names owner as part of the identity -- and nothing anywhere deduplicated: `sortFindings` (`preflight.go:200`) is a total order over `(Code, Field, Message)` that collapses nothing, and `simcontract.Assemble` did a straight `clone(in.Findings)`, with eight independent append sites feeding findings across the domain. Ordering was therefore already deterministic and was left alone; the half of RED about ordering changing across reloads did not reproduce. `Finding` now carries `Owner` and `CorroboratedBy`, and `DeduplicateFindings` groups by a typed `FindingIdentity` of `(Code, Field, Severity)` before presentation, never on rendered strings, picking the canonical `Message` deterministically so replay order cannot change the surviving explanation. `Owner` is deliberately outside the identity: two owners reporting one `(Code, Field, Severity)` are independently sourced corroboration of a single observation rather than two observations, so they collapse to one row whose every contributing owner is recorded, while a same-owner repeat collapses with an empty `CorroboratedBy`. Dedup runs inside `Assemble`, strictly upstream of `deriveStatus` and `computeDigest` and therefore of `Persist`, so the digest cannot vary with how many times a rule happened to fire and the reloaded count is exactly the assembled one. **A first implementation of this todo was sent back, and the reason is worth recording.** It defined the identity as `(Field, Severity)` alone, excluding `Code` on the reasoning that RED's "swapped internal code and message" meant neither field could be trusted. That silently discarded genuinely distinct observations: `checkCompensation` (`rules.go`) raises both `CodeProposedAmountInvalid` and `CodeNotARaise` on `Field` `proposed.base` at `SeverityBlocking` for a single proposal carrying a present-but-zero proposed base against a positive current base, because the early return guards only `!currentOK || !proposedOK` and a zero amount leaves `proposedOK` true. Under that identity the two collapsed into one and the lexicographically smaller pair won, so the reviewer was told the amount was not a raise and never told it was invalid. The same collision shape exists on `target.grade` (`CodeTargetGradeRequired` and `CodeSameGrade`) and on `proposed.base.currency` (`CodeCurrencyRequired` and `CodeCurrencyChangeNotV0`), and nothing enforces that such pairs stay mutually exclusive as rules are added. `Code` is a small closed vocabulary of rule-assigned typed constants, not a display string, so it belongs in the identity; `Message` is the freeform field REFACTOR's "never on rendered strings" is about, and it stays out. RED's swapped case now resolves on its own terms: the same `Code` with differing wording is a true duplicate and collapses, while genuinely differing `Code` means two rules fired and both are surfaced honestly rather than reconciled by guessing which message belongs to which code -- which would be rendered-string matching one level up. The regression test drives the real `promotion.PreflightPromotion` over a real `PreflightRequest` rather than a hand-built literal, and asserts the fixture actually reproduces both codes before asserting both survive, so it cannot quietly become vacuous if the rules change. **I mutation-verified that fix myself rather than relying on the lane's report**: reverting `Finding.Identity()` to `(Field, Severity)` failed `real_compensation_findings_survive_distinct_codes_on_one_field` with `Findings on proposed.base after dedup = [...], want exactly 2` and `distinct_codes_sharing_field_and_severity_are_never_merged` likewise, and restoring the line returned the package to green. The PROPERTY test was rebuilt for the same trap it had fallen into -- it had passed under the broken identity because its generator only ever produced genuine duplicates -- and now seeds every trial with a confusable neighbour carrying a different `Code` on a shared field and severity, failing at trial 0 under the reverted identity. **Boundary.** Nothing yet wires real preflight output into `AssembleInput.Findings` (`managerchange/setup.go` never sets it), so the roughly forty `Finding{...}` sites in `rules.go`, `target_manager.go` and `target_position.go` were left with an empty `Owner` rather than speculatively tagged, and `journeyv1.Finding` on the wire carries only severity, code and message -- no field or owner -- so typed dedup structurally cannot happen at that layer and the BROWSER test instead pins that the render layer is a faithful passthrough preserving order and count without re-deduplicating on strings

title: Keep promotion review confirmations compact, visible and keyboard-stable
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: expanding Start, Approve or Reject pushes the final action below the viewport, moves unrelated sections, loses focus or makes Cancel the most visually prominent control
green: a shared review surface keeps employee, change, date, consequences and final action together; the action bar remains visible; focus enters and returns correctly; Escape cancels; reduced motion is honored; server latency produces an in-place busy state that prevents duplicate submission without collapsing geometry
refactor: Start, Approve, Reject, Withdraw and Cancel reuse one confirmation component with typed content props
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Browser`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Performance` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux010_test.go`), plus a second `TestTodo_PROMOUX_010_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux010_test.go`) proving the wiring; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 96.5% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`) and 87.4% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **RED reproduced live before any change** at 1024x768 on the Start path: clicking `Propose promotion for Peter` left the submit control at document top 1241 in a 768px viewport with `scrollY` 0 (473px below the fold), shifted two `<section>` elements by +37px and -54px while document height collapsed from 4984 to 1423, and dropped `document.activeElement` to `BODY`. The review surface contained exactly one button, so RED's fourth clause -- Cancel being the most prominent control -- was false only because no cancel affordance existed at all, and `keydown`/`Escape` dispatched at both `document` and `document.body` changed nothing. **Verified live after the change, as this section's preamble requires**, rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. One `reviewSurface` component now serves every consequential action through typed content props, keeping the pre-existing `<details>`/`<summary>` disclosure byte-for-byte as the zero-JS baseline so `TestConsequentialActionRequiresAReviewDisclosure` passes unmodified, and using GWC's own `ui.Overlay` modal primitive for the focus trap rather than hand-rolling one. Opening it moves nothing outside itself: `sectionsMoved` 0 with document height 1427 before and after, the surface computing `position:fixed`, `max-height:736px` (100vh minus 2rem) and `overflow-y:auto`, its action bar holding Cancel at 3232px² against Submit at 7101px² so the destructive-adjacent control is 2.2x the visual weight of cancel, both at top 634 and inside the viewport. `Escape` closes it completely: `details.open` false, the surface removed, document height unchanged and `document.activeElement` back to `SUMMARY#propose-review-trigger` with focus returned to the exact trigger that opened it. **Three passes were sent back, and the reasons are the record.** The first built the component but wired it to nothing: `Action.Confirmation` was set in `projector.go` for Approve and Reject while `ProposalForm.Confirmation` was set by no caller at all, so the live Start path still rendered its submit in a plain `div.jn-formfoot` with zero `<details>` and zero `[class*=confirm]` elements -- the lane had reasoned that wiring lay outside this todo's Refs, and Refs name where work centers rather than fencing an unrendered component into a closed todo. The second wired it but left the entry point unreachable: after the fix the surface's own trigger sat at top 1252 with `scrollY` 0, 484px below the fold and within 5px of the original defect, so the clause stood. The third targeted focus at the page heading, which could never have closed it -- the heading renders at top 143, already inside the viewport and above the trigger, so focusing it cannot scroll anything into view; that was established by measuring both positions rather than by argument, and separately by confirming that one `.focus()` on the trigger itself moved `scrollY` from 0 to 666 and brought it to top 586 through the browser's own scroll-on-focus, with no scroll call. **The fourth pass also found why the effect had not been firing at all, and it is a genuine GWC hazard this repository already documents.** GWC hooks are positional and attach to `GetCurrentFiber()`, and only a `ui.CreateElement` boundary creates a fiber -- a plain nested function call does not. The focus hook had been invoked as a plain call inside `proposalView`, itself reached only through `LiveComponent.Build`'s `List`/`Proposal`/`Detail` switch, so it landed in whatever slot that single flat hook sequence happened to reach on a render whose shape changes with every page transition; `live.go`'s own doc comment warns about exactly this. Wrapping it as `ui.CreateElement(focusOnMount, ...)` gives it its own reconciled fiber. Live, the effect now fires on the `Page.List` to `Page.Proposal` swap: `document.activeElement` is `SUMMARY#propose-review-trigger`, `scrollY` is 659, and the trigger sits at top 587 inside the viewport, against `BODY` and top 1252 before. The page heading keeps its id and `tabindex="-1"` for screen-reader route announcement, which is the right target for that job and the wrong one for this geometry. The lane also caught a vacuous assertion in its own test while mutation-checking: retargeting the focus id back to the heading left the markup subtest passing, because both ids exist in the output regardless of which one the effect is told to focus, so a `focusOnMountHook` spy was added to assert the argument rather than the rendered ids -- the same build-it-but-do-not-wire-it shape as the first pass, caught one level down. **Residuals, named rather than smoothed over.** Clicking Start still swaps `Page.List` to `Page.Proposal` wholesale (document height 4971 to 1427); re-architecting that spans `journeywasm` routing, is high blast-radius, and is deliberately not this todo -- what this todo fixes is that the review-and-submit step reached by that swap is now contained, cancellable, keyboard-stable and in view. `Action.Busy` and `ProposalForm.Busy` are real tested props but no production caller sets them yet, so GREEN's in-place busy state is structurally present and not yet live; wiring it belongs where `journeyclient`'s store turns an `OnSubmit` click into an RPC and back, is not part of PROMOUX-013's authorization semantics, and is filed separately. Reduced motion is covered by the sheet's existing blanket `prefers-reduced-motion` rule rather than a new one

title: Invalidate promotion counts and timestamps after every durable transition
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: after creating or approving a promotion the shell still announces zero journeys, `Updated` remains older than the newest transition, or views converge only after unrelated navigation
green: each committed promotion transition emits one authority-filtered invalidation with sequence; shell count, Journeys, My Work, Person and detail refresh only their affected regions; displayed last-updated time equals the latest business transition; reconnect catch-up converges without duplicate renders or lost scroll/focus
refactor: consumers share cache keys and sequence handling; no page triggers a full-shell reload to achieve consistency
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Performance` in `internal/domains/promotion` (`promoux011_test.go`, `promoux011_performance_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Race` in `internal/data/promotioninvalidation` (`sequence_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Browser` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`promoux011_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_011_Recovery` in `tools/uxqual/invalidation` (`promoux011_test.go`); new `migrations/00288_promoux011_transition_sequence.sql`, `internal/data/promotioninvalidation` and `internal/domains/promotion/promoux011.go`. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 79.4% (`internal/domains/promotion`), 88.9% (`internal/data/promotioninvalidation`), 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 86.6% (`tools/uxqual/invalidation`), 81.7% (`internal/data/schema`), 100.0% (`internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`) and 81.5% (`migrations`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and driftgate and apigate pass on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test file was edited. The clause that carries this todo is that an authority-filtered invalidation carries a sequence, and those two requirements interact as a disclosure bug rather than a cosmetic one: with a global sequence and a filter that merely drops undeliverable messages, a viewer who observes 1, 2, 4 has learned that event 3 exists and can count promotions they hold no authority over. The scheme chosen is gap-free renumbering per subscriber. `promotioninvalidation.NextSequence` allocates each committed transition a durable global position through `INSERT ... ON CONFLICT ... DO UPDATE ... RETURNING`, evaluated inside each writer's own commit so concurrent writers cannot lose or duplicate one, but that value never reaches the wire -- it serves only as an item's revision for stale and reorder protection. `SubscriberSequencer.EmitForSubscriber` mints each subscriber its own counter and advances it by exactly one **only when a message is actually delivered**, so a transition authorising nothing for that subscriber never touches their counter and their visible sequence is contiguous by construction. The proof reproduces the leak before fixing it, which is what distinguishes it from a test that merely asserts the corrected behaviour: the PRIMARY's `subscriber_sequencer_closes_the_disclosure_gap_the_naive_scheme_leaks` subtest first runs the naive scheme and observes the delivered pair `[1, 3]` with a gap of 2, then runs the real one and requires `[1, 2]` with a delta of exactly 1. Region isolation is proven against real `tools/uxqual/invalidation.Client` instances rather than a stub: a Detail-region message for one worker fires exactly the matching client once and leaves a My-Work client and a different worker's Detail client at zero, so REFACTOR's prohibition on a full-shell reload is enforced rather than assumed. Last-updated is proven equal to the newest transition's own `OccurredAt` regardless of input order, with an empty set rendering an empty string rather than falling back to the current time. The no-duplicate-render clause is counted rather than inferred, because a double render converges to the same state and would pass any state assertion: the Recovery test counts `Refetch` invocations across a reconnect that redelivers an already-applied sequence before a genuinely new one, and requires exactly two. The Performance entry asserts delivered-message counts and bounded per-subscriber state rather than elapsed time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable wall-clock behaviour. Zero values fail closed throughout: `RegionCursor{}` refuses any incoming value including 0, `Transition{}` and zero-revision or zero-timestamp variants fail `Validate()`, and the sequencer never advances on an undelivered message. **A defect I introduced was found by this lane and corrected here.** The `ledger_payload_disposition` row I added during PROMOUX-002 review declared `data_role: EVIDENCE` and `retention_class: EVIDENCE`, neither of which is a declared value -- `data_role` admits only LEDGER, PROJECTION, OUTBOX, REGISTRY, CONTROL and AGGREGATE, and `retention_class` only PERMANENT, OPERATIONAL and REBUILDABLE. It broke `TestTodo_STORE_001` and `TestTodo_STORE_001_Mutation` and had escaped notice because that gate lives in `internal/data/tenancy/storagedisposition`, a different package from the `TestTodo_DATA_001` check run at the time. Corrected to LEDGER and PERMANENT, matching `ledger_event` itself. **Boundaries.** The components are not wired into a live promotion page, the same boundary PROMOUX-003, 005, 006 and 007 recorded and which is escalated for all of them together; no production caller yet invokes `NextSequence` from a committed-transition write path, which lies outside this todo's Refs. DOM scroll and focus preservation on reconnect is asserted structurally -- region containers are independently addressable -- because it cannot be proven in a non-browser Go test, and the Recovery test says so in its own comment

title: Distinguish actionable approvals, tracked promotions and passive waits
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: My Work says every visible journey needs attention while listing a future-date wait with no action, or Person omits an active promotion while offering a duplicate start
green: My Work contains assigned decisions and tasks with owner, due date and next action; Tracked requests contains promotions the viewer initiated or follows; passive waits show next transition and owner without inflating actionable counts; Person displays active and past workflows with direct resume/open links
refactor: all surfaces consume the same server-resolved relationship-to-viewer and next-action projection
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_012` (PRIMARY) in `internal/intent/app`, `internal/transport/journey`, `internal/humanwork/productui`, `tools/uxqual/productclient` and `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_012_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_012_Security` (embedded PostgreSQL through `NewCell`, the real intent store and journey engine) in `internal/intent/app`; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_012_Browser`, `_Accessibility` and `TestPersonActiveWorkflowsOrderFallbackAndEmptyState` in `internal/humanwork/productui`; `TestTodo_PROMOUX_012_Regression` in `productui`, `productclient` and `journeyclient`; `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths` extended to the tracking line and Person section lines; no migration. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS for productui (93.5%), productclient (85.0%), journeyclient (84.3%), render/journey (96.5%), transport/journey (80.6%), humanwork/workspace (62.8%, existing exception), journeywasm (83.0%) and intent/app (52.2%, existing exception), plus `internal/application`'s UXAUDIT-017 and PROMOUX-013 integration tests, all re-run by the orchestrator; `go build ./...`, native and js/wasm `go vet` clean; `go run ./tools/policy/apigate/cmd/apigate -root .` PASS with no endpoint-manifest change; `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. **REFACTOR's single projection:** `Journey.viewer` (field 21) is resolved server-side in `internal/intent/app/journey_viewer_projection.go` from the intent's stored initiator and the work-item membership UXAUDIT-017 already computes, naming only the viewer's own relationship (INITIATOR, ASSIGNEE, CANDIDATE) and a responsibility of ACTION_REQUIRED (holds or may claim the item, or initiated it and the next step is theirs, such as correcting a blocked proposal), TRACKING (initiated it while someone else or the workflow holds the next step), OBSERVING or CLOSED, plus the next step, its owner and closure; Every surface consumes it: one `journeyclient.StagePresentation` table replaced the two disagreeing status vocabularies (Journeys now uses My Work's wording) and the client-side stage table was removed. **My Work** defaults to `Needs your action`, containing only work the viewer must act on, and the navigation badge and notification count use the same set, so passive waits no longer inflate actionable counts and the page no longer says every journey needs attention; `Awaiting approval` now selects actionable items by server next-step code (generic, manager, finance or repeat approval) instead of the literal label, and Insights' `Needs attention` had the same label-matching defect and was fixed the same way; a new `Tracked requests` tab (`filter=tracked`) holds promotions the viewer initiated, with rows the viewer is only tracking stating `No action needed from you` and passive waits showing their next step and `Waiting on the workflow`. **Person** gains an `Active workflows` section above past workflows linking each open journey as Resume when the viewer must act and Open otherwise; PROMOUX-002's launcher suppression already existed, but the utility drawer's `Available actions` still offered Start promotion with a promotion in flight -- it now links to the active promotion and offers no start for ineligible workers -- and an open journey now blocks Start in the launcher and People rows even when eligibility says otherwise, matching journeys named by entity reference too. **Live verification** on the rebuilt cell (wasm bundle hash matched its manifest): as `hc-054-thomas-baker`, `Needs your action` narrowed from seven journeys to his two finance approvals, each with `Your next action: Claim`, `Assigned to you` and `Due 2026-09-15`, and the count label read 2 items; as the admin persona, who initiated all seven, `Needs your action` held exactly the two BLOCKED proposals awaiting correction, `Tracked requests` held all seven with `No action needed from you` on the five whose next step belongs to finance or the workflow, and `Awaiting approval` was correctly empty because the admin cannot act on either finance approval; at 390px the tracking line rendered, only `.row-summary` was hidden and nothing scrolled horizontally. Four golden digests were re-pinned (WEB-037, WEB-039, WEB-042, WEB-063), each after reproducing the previous digest byte for byte by substituting back exactly the old notification and subtitle copy or omitting the new empty Active workflows section. Nineteen mutations were killed by name, including an initiator's own step not actionable, a passive wait marked actionable, any initiator treated as the viewer (Security), the list ignoring the initiator (Integration), the projection dropped at transport, My Work or the badge or notifications counting all open journeys, label-matched approvals, the drawer offering Start, and the tracking line hidden at narrow width. Recorded limits: nothing records followers, so Tracked requests covers initiated promotions only and `follows` would need a follower store and a follow affordance; REPAIR_REQUIRED journeys appear in nobody's My Work because nothing records a repair owner (the initiator sees them under Tracked requests); the SUBJECT relationship is not built because no trusted principal-to-worker link exists on the list path; and the Integration and Security tests exercise Propose, List and Inspect but not Execute. title: Add governed edit, supersede, withdraw and cancel paths
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: a proposer cannot correct an unstarted proposal, withdraw before approval, or request cancellation during an eligible wait; or an edit silently changes an approved revision
green: authorized edits create a new proposal revision and invalidate material approvals; withdrawal and cancellation use typed interventions with reasons, consequence preview and retained evidence; unavailable stages explain why; races with approval, timer and terminal commit resolve to one deterministic outcome with no partial domain write
refactor: UI actions map to existing intent and intervention semantics; no delete or in-place proposal update
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux013_test.go`) and in `internal/transport/journey` (`promoux013_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Security` in `internal/transport/journey`, `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Integration` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Race` in `internal/application` (`promoux013_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Browser`, `_Accessibility` and `_I18N` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux013_test.go`), and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_ClientServerAvailabilityAgreement` in `internal/intent/app` (`promoux013_agreement_test.go`); no migration required, but this todo does change the wire contract. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 45.4% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception), 80.2% (`internal/transport/journey`), 84.2% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`), 96.6% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 83.0% (`tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm`) and 62.8% (`internal/humanwork/workspace`, under its recorded exception); `go test -count=1 ./test/tunnel/...` PASS in 259s; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED and `npm run check:apigate` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. Three RPCs were added to `JourneyService` -- `EditProposal`, `PreviewJourneyIntervention` (read-only) and `RequestJourneyIntervention` -- each carrying the file's own `Effect class:` disposition comment verified through a descriptor-based totality test, plus a shared `hcmnext.common.v1.InterventionOutcome` enum (`APPLIED|PENDING_SAFE_POINT|DENIED|TOO_LATE|REPAIR_REQUIRED`) and `Journey.governance_version`, the intent's own optimistic-concurrency version, which nothing on this wire exposed before. `buf generate` is byte-identical across two runs and touches only the three expected files, independently reproduced at review time by regenerating and comparing digests. The wire change was necessary because `DecideJourneyRequest` carried only `{intent_id, approve bool, reason}` -- an approve/reject binary with no room for withdraw, cancel, supersede or edit. **The implementation reused the existing domain capability rather than reimplementing it, and discovering that `SupersedeIntent` could not be reused at all was the key finding.** `promote_worker` is P1A/`simulateOnlyChangeTransitions`, whose `SUPERSEDED` edges exist only from `SIMULATED`, `SUBMITTED` or `APPROVED`; a journey's stored intent never durably leaves `DRAFT`, and the kernel's own lifecycle profile has no `DRAFT` to `SUPERSEDED` edge, so `SupersedeIntent` is structurally unusable here. `EditProposal` therefore composes `CancelIntent` -- legal from `DRAFT` and already safe-point-aware for a mid-flight `EXECUTING` journey -- followed by an ordinary `Propose` once the cancellation disposition is genuinely `CANCELLED`, which makes GREEN's requirement that edits create a new proposal revision and invalidate material approvals literally true: the original carries the approval, the original is what is durably cancelled, and the successor inherits nothing. **Three real defects were found by running the code rather than reasoning about it, each observed failing before the fix and passing after.** `lifecycle_endpoints.go`'s `SupersedeIntent` minted and durably appended the successor intent before validating and applying the original's own transition, so a refused or raced supersede left an orphaned successor behind -- a genuine partial write, now reordered so the original's compare-and-swap lands first. `journey_decide.go`'s `Decide` and `Execute` checked no terminal `RequestState`, so a journey cancelled mid-flight could still be decided or executed; both now carry a terminal-state guard. And `internal/data/promotionguard.Release` was dead code by its own doc comment, so a cancelled-then-reproposed journey for the same worker and effective date would have refused itself as a duplicate; it is now called on a successful `CANCELLED` disposition. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_Race` drives 8 concurrent goroutines -- 4 `EditProposal`, 4 `RequestJourneyIntervention(WITHDRAW)` -- through the production connection pool against one real proposed journey, all presenting the same expected version, and asserts durable state rather than return codes: exactly one successor intent exists if an edit won and zero if a withdraw won, which is what would have caught the orphaned-successor defect directly. The UI is wired end to end rather than left as an unreachable capability: `reviewSurface` needed no changes because PROMOUX-010's prop contract was deliberately built to accommodate Withdraw and Cancel, so this was plumbing through `journeyclient`, and Withdraw, Cancel and Edit render at every stage -- disabled with a named reason when unavailable rather than omitted, since an omitted action is indistinguishable from one that does not exist. `interventionNotice` reports the typed outcome truthfully instead of always claiming cancellation. The disclosure rule is proven by value in the I18N test, which asserts the disabled-reason text is byte-identical across two journeys sharing a terminal stage but differing in worker name and correlation id -- the same pattern PROMOUX-001 and PROMOUX-004 established. **A client-side mirror of the server's stage-availability rule was accepted but required a test, and the lane was sent back for it.** `journeyclient.InterventionAvailability` mirrors `internal/intent/app`'s unexported `interventionUnavailableAtStage` so availability cannot go stale between watch pushes; it is a presentation hint rather than an authorization decision, since the server refuses on submit regardless, but an untested mirror drifts silently and the failure mode is a user confidently told an action is unavailable when it is not. `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_ClientServerAvailabilityAgreement` now runs both implementations across the full cross product of 15 stages by 2 kinds, reading the stage and kind lists from the generated enums' own `_name` maps rather than a hardcoded list so a newly added stage fails the test instead of being silently skipped, with a hard failure if either map is empty or names a kind the test does not cover; all 30 pairs agree on both availability and reason reference. Mutation-verified by dropping `stageBlocked` from the client's unstarted check, which failed exactly two pairs by name -- `WITHDRAW at BLOCKED` and `CANCEL at BLOCKED` -- while the other 28 kept passing. The three UI tests were each mutation-verified too: dropping `DisabledReason` failed the BROWSER naming `disabled action "withdraw" has no reason paragraph`; renaming the reason field's label and dropping `Required` failed the ACCESSIBILITY naming `no visible label "Reason" found`; and forcing the static description in place of the server preview failed the I18N naming that the server-worded consequence summary did not survive rendering byte-for-byte. **Boundaries, recorded rather than glossed.** The I18N test proves the plumbing survives translated and bidi content but does not prove localized delivery, because `tools/uxqual/render/journey` has no locale catalog and emits no `dir="rtl"` anywhere -- every string including PROMOUX-010's is fixed English Go source, and building that catalog is a separate and much larger effort. Consequence previews refresh on detail load and after an intervention rather than on every watch tick, so the server's worded consequence sentence has a bounded staleness window; availability and reason text never go stale, being computed from the always-fresh stage. Edit's job-code and base-pay fields pre-fill from display strings rather than parsed values, which is cosmetic because the reviewer retypes them. `EP-WF-002` was deliberately not implemented, but `InterventionOutcome` and `workspace.JourneyInterventionOutcome` are placed in shared locations specifically so its Pause, Resume, Cancel and RetryNode work can adopt the same five-value vocabulary rather than inventing a second one. **One infrastructure landmine was found and independently reproduced:** `buf.gen.yaml` declares `clean: true` over the whole `gen/go` tree, which also holds `gen/go/hcmnext/model/model_generated.go`, a non-buf output from `tools/gen/modelgen`, so every `buf generate` silently deletes it -- verified at review time by running `buf generate` and watching the file disappear, then restoring it byte-identical with `go run ./tools/gen/modelgen/cmd/modelgen`. That is the true cause of a phantom missing-`gen/go/hcmnext/model` build failure another lane hit earlier the same day, which was initially misattributed to a concurrency race. It needs a permanent fix -- a combined regeneration script or a separate output root -- and is filed separately rather than patched here

title: Explain effective-date waits and provide a bounded local-dev completion path
section: 70. Promotion workflow live-audit remediation
red: `Waiting for effective date` gives no next timestamp, timezone, owner, scheduled action or explanation, and the supported local-dev profile cannot exercise terminal recording without waiting for wall-clock time
green: the waiting state names the effective instant and timezone, what will run, remaining checks, notification behavior and any authorized intervention; production exposes no manual timer bypass; a separately fenced local-dev clock/driver can advance a same-day fixture through END and is impossible to enable under a production profile
refactor: the UI reads typed WAIT resolution and profile capabilities; it never manufactures countdown or completion authority
evidence: `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) in `internal/intent/app` (`wait_explain_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Integration` in `internal/application` (`promoux014_integration_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Recovery` in `internal/application` (`promoux014_recovery_test.go`, `//go:build devtools`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Security` in `internal/platform/devclock` (`promoux014_security_test.go`), `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Browser` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey` (`promoux014_test.go`) and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_014_Regression` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (`promoux014_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 46.1% (`internal/intent/app`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised from 45.4% by this change), 100.0% (`internal/platform/devclock` default build), 96.6% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 87.5% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`), 94.4% (`internal/workflow/promotionexec`) and 81.3% (`internal/application`); `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go build -tags devtools ./internal/platform/devclock/` and `go vet -tags devtools` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **RED reproduced live before the change.** A `WAITING_EFFECTIVE_DATE` card on the running server rendered only `Waiting for effective date`, the placement and pay lines, `Effective 1 Dec 2026` and `Updated 2026-09-13 08:25 UTC`: of RED's five facts the next timestamp was a bare date rather than an instant, and the timezone, owner, scheduled action and explanation were absent outright. Three journeys sit in that stage, so the gap was against real data rather than a fixture. The second half reproduced too -- a sweep of non-test code for a clock driver found only `internal/data/health`'s `FakeClock`, a health-projection concern, and a doc-comment mention in `internal/platform/timeauth`, so nothing could advance a promotion's wait and the local-dev profile could not reach terminal recording without wall-clock time. All five facts are now server-sourced and none is computed in the browser: the instant and timezone come from the durable pending timer's `FiresAt` (`internal/workflow/timer.Scheduler.Pending`) paired with `promotionexec.EffectiveDateZoneID`, verified against the real engine to resolve a `2026-06-01` effective date to `2026-06-01T04:00:00Z` under America/New*York; the owner is the latest completed `APPROVAL` work item's `CompletedBy`; the scheduled action is read from `promotionexec.Definition().Edges`' real `FIRED` route out of the wait node rather than hardcoded prose; and the remaining checks, notification behaviour and intervention statements describe what the engine actually does. The proposer is deliberately **not** shown as owner, because that would require `IntentInstance.Initiator`, which has no wire slot on `Journey` or `JourneyDetail` -- named rather than approximated. Because `schema/proto` and `gen/` are frozen, the six facts travel as `WAIT*\*`codes through the existing generic`JourneyDetail.Findings`vessel, and the client filters them out of the generic preflight board into their own labelled subsection instead of letting them inflate it. **The fence is the security-critical half and is structural, not merely checked.** The driver lives behind a`devtools`build tag: the default`driver_stub.go`never imports`timer.Scheduler.Fire`, so the capability is absent from `cmd/hcmnext`'s ordinary build, from CI and from the amd64 cross-compile, rather than present and refused. `devprofile.Name`-gated construction is defence in depth on top, fail-closed with exact-match only, and an unexported `ready`field leaves even a hand-constructed`Driver{}`literal inert. The driver wraps exactly the production`timer.Scheduler.Fire`and`executionscheduler.Scheduler.Tick`path rather than duplicating engine logic. All six tests were mutation-verified: removing the`Kind != KindApproval`filter in`lastApprovalOwner`failed the PRIMARY naming the leak; disabling the`Inspect`attach block emptied all six findings and failed the INTEGRATION; changing the subsection heading failed the BROWSER; making the stub's`fireNow`branch on tenant failed the SECURITY's byte-identical check; dropping`.Add(ahead)`from the dev clock failed the RECOVERY with`Fired 0 want 1`; and removing the all-codes-present guard in `waitExplanationFacts`failed the REGRESSION on both its partial and absent sub-cases. **Live-verification boundary, recorded rather than glossed.** Unlike section 69, this section carries no direct-browser-evidence requirement, and three independent constraints blocked a live read of the rendered panel: signing in from the browser pane is refused with`the request origin is not allowed`, because the pane's sandboxed iframe Origin fails `originAllowed`; `/workspace/journey` runs under a fixed local-dev identity (`hc-054-thomas-baker`, `promotion_operator`) whose organization scope cannot open any of the three waiting journeys, each answering `This journey is unavailable`; and the Connect RPC is not exposed on the plain HTTP listener, answering `404`at`/hcmnext.journey.v1.JourneyService/InspectJourney`because it is reachable only through the`/workspace/grpc`tunnel. The INTEGRATION test against real PostgreSQL is therefore what proves the server attaches these findings on real data, and the BROWSER test is what proves the renderer displays them. **Gap, named:** the driver is not wired into`serve.go`or`handler.go`-- both fenced off this session by another todo's uncommitted work -- so today it is consumable through`go test -tags devtools` rather than a CLI

red: GAP contradicting `WEB-092` ("Implement the sanitized content editor," ticked green): `EditBindingContent`'s `containsRawMarkup` only refuses `<` followed by a letter, `/`, `!`, or `?` and explicitly punts "entities, URLs, origins" to publication-time "content-safety gates" (`internal/humanwork/productui/content_editor.go:29-35`); `PublishGoverned` (`internal/humanwork/productui/page_draft.go:109-139`) only runs `ValidateComposition` (purpose/floorplan/regions/widgets/actions/ceiling), `ValidatePreviewPlan`, preview-evidence equality, and reviewer-approval checks — none of which inspect `WidgetBinding.Value`/`DisplayValue` content. `grep -rn "func Sanitize\|ContentSafety" --include=*.go .` returns nothing repo-wide, and `ValidateWidgetBinding` (`internal/humanwork/productui/widget.go`) checks only registry/version/classification/masked-display, never value content. refactor: fold the new check into `ValidateComposition`'s `ValidationStep` set rather than bolting a second ad hoc gate onto `PublishGoverned`, so validation-panel and publication share one authoritative content-safety finding

title: Select and evidence the first legal jurisdiction and bounded rule-pack scope
section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: selection lacks authoritative source citations, qualified legal owner/reviewer, included intent/rule/filing set, effective and known-at interval, collective/company interaction, uncertainty behavior, update SLA, prohibited legal-advice boundary or stop/reselect threshold
green: signed jurisdiction profile pins sources and versions, maps every Phase 1 legal input/decision/obligation/evidence path, declares exact exclusions and returns `UNKNOWN|HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED` instead of guessing outside the reviewed scope
refactor: selection supplies data to LegalContext and regulatory-pack publication; it never hard-codes law in workflow branches
evidence: `TestPilotJurisdictionSelectionHasAuthoritativeSourcesReviewScopeAndStopConditions` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus the `_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Security`, `_Conformance` and `_UncertaintyBehavior` tests in `tools/planning/pilotjurisdiction`, and `tools/planning/cmd/pilotjurisdiction`'s own tests; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 81.6% (`tools/planning/pilotjurisdiction`) and 80.6% (`tools/planning/cmd/pilotjurisdiction`), both above the floor; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **The pilot jurisdiction is California**, chosen by Cam from the two `LEGAL-001` already seeded. The profile is `definitions/planning/gates/select-001-jurisdiction-profile.yaml`, following `PHASE-001`'s `scopeceiling` conventions exactly -- a JSON-projection `CanonicalDigest` over every field except the signature, ed25519 signing reused from `gateevidence.SignDigest`/`VerifyDigestSignature` rather than new crypto, and a consumer CLI so the artifact is read by something. It pins two sources by content digest, both cross-checked live against disk in the CONFORMANCE test: `planning/research/state-employment-law/california.md` at `daed211f...5f87`, and `definitions/legal/packs/states/us-ca.json` (`us-ca-promotion-base-pay-change-draft`, version 1.0, vocabulary 2, `review_status: UNREVIEWED`) at `ae83ff79...c92b`. Exclusions are declared exactly rather than gestured at: all 22 `legal.ObligationType` kinds are partitioned into 18 mapped -- the kinds the pinned California pack actually populates -- and four excluded by name with reasons (`E_VERIFY`, `JOB_SECURITY`, `SEPARATION_FILING`, `AUTOMATED_DECISION`), plus a `JURISDICTION` exclusion covering every state but California and a `LOCALITY` exclusion recording that the pinned pack is state-level with an empty `locality_path`. `Validate` rejects any kind that is both mapped and excluded or neither, and the conformance test cross-checks the partition against the live pack's own `KindCounts()` rather than against the profile's bookkeeping. **It binds to `LegalContext` rather than duplicating it, which is what REFACTOR asks:** `Authorize` calls `legal.Resolve` directly, so a genuinely contradictory input -- on-site California work asserted against a New York employment jurisdiction -- fails exactly as `legal.Resolve` fails, wrapped in `legal.ErrLegalContextUnknown` and mapped to `HUMAN_REVIEW_REQUIRED`; a confident resolution to any jurisdiction other than California returns `UNKNOWN` with a new `ErrOutsideReviewedScope`, never silently applying California's rules elsewhere. Obligation-to-intent bindings read lifecycle step and binding kind live from `legal.ObligationKindSpecFor` instead of restating them. **The profile is unreviewed, deliberately and structurally.** RED requires a qualified legal owner and reviewer and no such person is recorded anywhere in the repository, so rather than fabricating a name into a signed governance artifact the reviewer is a required field that `Validate` rejects when empty: the checked-in file reports exactly one violation, `reviewer.name: missing`, asserted precisely by the PRIMARY test, and the profile carries `review_status: UNREVIEWED`. This mirrors how the repository already models unverified legal content -- the California pack itself ships `UNREVIEWED` with a `-draft` pack id -- and matches `PHASE-001`'s empty-selection-slot treatment. It also leaves `PHASE-001`'s `jurisdiction` slot untouched and unfilled, because filling it is `NEXT-002`'s job and that ceiling's own security test proves a quietly filled slot invalidates its signature. Six mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored: disabling the reviewer-required check failed the PRIMARY and `Property/reviewer_name_missing`; disabling the obligation-coverage loop failed `Property/obligation_kind_neither_mapped_nor_excluded` while the deliberately `Validate`-independent CONFORMANCE test correctly kept passing; dropping `ReviewStatus` from the digest payload failed both GOLDEN and SECURITY; forcing `VerifyProfileSignature` to return true failed all seven SECURITY tamper subtests; disabling the out-of-scope jurisdiction check failed only the `returns_UNKNOWN` subtest with the other two correctly unaffected; and suppressing violation printing in the CLI failed its report test. One test-authoring error was found and fixed along the way -- a `wantHit` substring that did not match the actual violation message in two subtests -- and was a test bug rather than a production one

The implementation therefore makes the fabrication structurally impossible to mistake for fact, reusing this repository's own convention for unverified content rather than inventing one. **No real company is named as the provider.** `vendor_id` is `legacyhcm-incumbent-PLACEHOLDER-UNVERIFIED` and `vendor_display_name` is `Unselected Incumbent Core HCM (Workday-class placeholder, not a real vendor)`; the only occurrences of real vendor names in the artifact are a citation of `specs/integration-platform.md`'s own wording (`likely Workday or an equivalent incumbent`) and its Core HCM connector family list, plus that self-disclaiming display string. Enforcement lives in `Validate`, not in comments: `selection_status` is a closed field over `PLACEHOLDER_UNVERIFIED` and `VENDOR_CONFIRMED`, and while placeholder, `Validate` rejects any `vendor_id` lacking the mandatory `-PLACEHOLDER-UNVERIFIED` suffix and rejects any populated field in `vendor_confirmation`, so no partial claim of confirmation is representable. Flipping to `VENDOR_CONFIRMED` requires both that the suffix is gone and that contact, contract reference and signed date are all present. **The placeholder is provably incapable of satisfying a real selection gate, by value rather than by flag.** `SatisfiesRealProviderSelectionGate` is deliberately independent of `Validate`, and its test proves three things: the checked-in file fails on five named grounds; flipping only `selection_status` to `VENDOR_CONFIRMED` still fails, because the vendor-id suffix and the empty confirmation values keep it failing; and only a fully consistent swap of status, real vendor id and complete confirmation passes. Note the deliberate contrast with `SELECT-001`, whose profile carries exactly one violation because its reviewer field is genuinely missing: here `Validate` returns zero violations, because the artifact is a structurally honest and complete placeholder rather than a broken document, and its incompleteness is expressed through the separate gate instead. The fault matrix covers `specs/integration-platform.md`'s nine error-taxonomy classes exactly once each, from `AUTHENTICATION` through `FINAL_BUSINESS_REJECT`, each with a distinct example response, default action and evidence reference pointing at `PROVIDER-001`'s real fixtures in `internal/connectivity/providercontract`; the test asserts exactness -- no duplicated class, no copy-pasted action -- rather than mere non-emptiness. Sandbox evidence declares `SYNTHETIC_FIXTURE_ONLY` fidelity and states plainly that no real vendor sandbox tenant exists. **REFACTOR's provider-neutrality is enforced by a real scan rather than asserted:** `ScanForIdentityLeak` walks the live `internal/` tree, excluding `internal/connectivity` as the adapter boundary and `internal/generated`, looking for the vendor identifier, and finds zero hits today. Its limitation is stated in the test's own doc comment rather than left implicit: it proves no current direct textual reference exists outside the adapter boundary, not the stronger claim that no code could branch on any provider identity through indirect means, which would need data-flow analysis. Every test was mutation-verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored: hardcoding `SatisfiesRealProviderSelectionGate` to true broke the PRIMARY, INTEGRATION and placeholder-gate tests; disabling `Validate`'s product check broke exactly `Property/missing_product`; making `CanonicalDigest` constant broke all nine MUTATION subtests as not byte-detectable; hardcoding the wrong TodoID in `payload()` broke GOLDEN on digest mismatch; forcing `VerifyTopologySignature` true broke all nine SECURITY tamper cases; dropping a class from `AllFaultClasses()` broke the FAULT exactness subtest; and corrupting the CONFORMANCE expectation broke its live cross-check against the real `phase1-scope-ceiling.yaml`, proving that check is not vacuous. Two of those mutations deserve their own note. Making `ScanForIdentityLeak` return nil broke its own planted-reference test and, separately, demonstrated that the main REFACTOR test would return a **false negative** on exactly that defect -- disclosed rather than hidden. And swapping the scan's needle for a guaranteed-common word confirmed the walk genuinely reaches real files, returning thousands of hits, while also confirming the `internal/connectivity` skip is real, since the similarly-named `internal/data/connectivityopstore` still surfaced. section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: any source→slice→model/engine/capability→handler→endpoint→scenario/test/todo/evidence edge is absent, duplicated, stale or aggregate-only while maturity advances
green: every source-bound definition has exactly one digest-backed witness containing all graph and reverse edges, phase/gate, endpoint disposition, test/evidence outputs and expiry; orphan/duplicate/stale edge returns `SLICE_CLOSURE_INCOMPLETE`

evidence: `TestPerIntentClosureWitnessCrossJoinIsTotalUniqueAndCurrent` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus `TestTodo_SLICE_016_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Security`, `_Conformance` and `_Mutation` in the new `tools/planning/closurewitness`, and `tools/planning/cmd/closurewitness`'s own tests; no migration. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 95.4% and 84.4%, re-run by the orchestrator; `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. `Compile` derives witnesses only from registry rows read by `LoadSnapshot` -- intent descriptors (the source authority left after `SOURCE-001` retired), `definitions.All`, the scope ceiling, product slices, `modelbinding`, `enginecoverage`, `BIND-001`'s claims and binding table, `PROTO-010`/`ENDPOINT-009` dispositions and the endpoint manifest, `workflowmaturity` scenario matrices, `todos.md` via `coveragematrix`, `capability-coverage.yaml`, test-name scans including `test/`, and evidence-freshness waivers -- and no input field carries a result or maturity, so closure cannot be asserted by hand. Each source-bound definition gets exactly one digest-backed witness with forward and reverse edges over twelve classes (source, phase/gate, slice, model, engine, capability, handler, endpoint, scenario, test, todo, evidence), endpoint disposition, test and evidence outputs, and an expiry equal to the earliest waiver it leans on or `NO_WAIVER`. Absent, reverse-absent, duplicate, stale, aggregate-only, orphan, unsourced and maturity-over-claim defects each return `SLICE_CLOSURE_INCOMPLETE` with an exact identity; a missing registry marks its class `UNSOURCED` instead of loading empty; `Verify` rejects tampered reports even with a recomputed per-witness digest; two runs over unchanged inputs are byte-identical. **Live, 0 of 14 source-bound definitions close**, with 61 orphan edges: every PHASE_GATE edge is STALE because maturity is claimed without closure, ENGINE is ABSENT for all 14 (declared engines not imported), HANDLER is ABSENT for 11 and DUPLICATE for 3, and ENDPOINT is AGGREGATE_ONLY for the eight P1A intents. The orphans are 31 unbound wire methods, 17 todos whose `INTENTS=` holds the display name `PromoteWorker` rather than a definition ref (`EP-PROMO-001`, `PROMOUX-001`–`015`, `UXAUDIT-002`), three `DIRECT` leave tokens in `NEXT-007`, eight registry-capability rows with no definition and two served RegistryService endpoints accepting no definition. One real stale edge was confirmed independently by the orchestrator: `UX-009`, ticked 2026-09-05, names PRIMARY `TestJourneyDrivesPromotionFromProposalToRecordedOutcome`, which is defined nowhere in the tree -- its Evidence cites five other tests, so the traceability gate, which reads Evidence names, never saw it. The complete fixture (two definitions) reaches COMPLETE; Mutation plants 25 defects and a branch test covers 62 rule and orphan shapes, each first asserting the base fixture lacks the defect so none is vacuous. Seven mutations were verified by name: an always-COMPLETE witness (PRIMARY), unsorted witnesses (Property), a changed schema version (Golden), `Verify` skipping per-witness comparison (Security, after tightening a substring that would have missed it), dispositions keyed by bare id (Conformance), waiver expiry never checked, and the shared-test aggregate check removed. Partial REFACTOR, recorded: `closurewitness.Summary` is a witness-only coverage view, but `tools/planning/designclosure` (CLOSE-001) does not yet consume witnesses, and its and `intentcoverage`'s loaders scan only `tools`, `internal`, `cmd` and `gen` for test names, missing `test/` -- a likely source of false dangling-test reports. Two rules are this package's own rather than a registry's (release-to-gate mapping P1A→P1A, P1B→P1B, CONFORMANCE→NONE; DEFINED maturity on an incomplete witness is a PHASE_GATE defect), and JUSTIFIED_ABSENT endpoints rest on a written justification with no recorded reviewer. No witness output is checked in, since it would drift on every `todos.md` edit
