title: Compile trust-boundary threat models for every Phase 1 vertical slice
section: 62. Product-decision and implementation convergence
red: slice omits actor/asset/trust boundary/data class/entry point/threat/mitigation/detection/recovery/owner/test, ignores confused deputy, tenant crossover, stale authorization, insider abuse, metadata leakage, replay, ambiguous effect, supply-chain or human-social attack, or marks accepted risk without expiry
green: generated threat register maps each slice graph edge to reviewed threats and controls, produces exact negative/security/fault tests, retains residual risk with accountable acceptance and expiry and blocks release for unmitigated critical findings
refactor: threat identities are stable and deduplicated by asset+boundary+attack; shared mitigations retain every consuming slice edge
evidence: `TestPhaseOneThreatModelCoversEveryTrustBoundaryAssetActorAndAbusePath` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field) plus the `_Property`, `_Golden`, `_Fault`, `_Security`, `_Conformance`, `_Mutation` and `_Refactor` tests and `FuzzTodo_THREAT_001` in `tools/planning/threatregister`, and `tools/planning/cmd/threatregister`'s own tests; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 87.4% (`tools/planning/threatregister`) and 72.7% (`tools/planning/cmd/threatregister`), both above the floor; `go build ./...` clean on windows/arm64 and cross-checked clean under `GOOS=linux GOARCH=amd64`, `go vet` and gofmt clean, `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The register is `definitions/planning/gates/threat-001-register.yaml`, enumerated against `phase1-scope-ceiling.yaml`'s INCLUDE dispositions rather than an invented slice set, and follows the conventions `PHASE-001`, `SELECT-001` and `SELECT-002` set earlier the same day -- a JSON-projection `CanonicalDigest` over every field except the signature, ed25519 signing reused from `gateevidence`, and a consumer CLI so the artifact is read by something. **REFACTOR is enforced on a real key rather than on a label:** `ThreatIdentity(sliceID, asset, trustBoundary, attackClass)` is the sole dedup key and a threat's free-text `ID` is explicitly never used for identity, with `Validate` flagging any identity appearing more than once. Shared-mitigation retention is checked by computing, per mitigation, the union of `ConsumingEdges` across every threat naming it and requiring the mitigation's declared edge list to equal that union exactly -- no drop and no over-claim -- and the real register exercises it rather than only a fixture, because `MIT-REVALIDATE-BEFORE-COMMIT` is genuinely shared between `THR-01` (`STALE_AUTHORIZATION`, EDGE-01) and `THR-06` (`REPLAY`, EDGE-06). Since the real file contains no duplicate identity, the dedup test builds a genuine one -- same asset, boundary and attack class, different ID and prose -- so the check is not vacuous. Attack-class coverage iterates `AllAttackClasses()`, the nine RED-named classes, as the single taxonomy source rather than a hardcoded list, proven by a test that removes each class in turn driven off that function, so a future tenth class gains coverage automatically. **The register's most consequential output is that it blocks Phase 1 release today.** `THR-07` (`AMBIGUOUS_EFFECT`, CRITICAL) is unmitigated because Phase 1 has not built the observe-before-retry mechanism, and it carries a real justification and expiry but no accepting owner, because none has been designated. Rather than fabricate an accountable party the field is required-and-empty, exactly as `SELECT-001`'s reviewer is: `Validate` reports precisely one violation, `slices[0].residual_risks[0].accepted_by`, and `ReleaseDecision(now)` -- deliberately independent of `Validate`, mirroring `pilotprovider`'s gate-versus-validate split so a structural fix cannot accidentally unblock a release -- reports `release blocked: true`. **An accountable owner must accept that residual risk, or the mitigation must be built, before Phase 1 can release.** The companion case the real file cannot reach is covered by fixture: an accepted-but-expired acceptance also fails to waive the block, so only an accepted and unexpired acceptance clears it. Seven mutations were verified, each broken, observed failing by name, then restored: disabling the attack-class coverage loop failed all nine PROPERTY subtests while leaving the PRIMARY unaffected because the real data is already total; disabling `ReleaseDecision`'s block condition failed the PRIMARY and both FAULT tests; disabling mitigation retention failed the MUTATION, PROPERTY and REFACTOR retention tests; disabling dedup failed the duplicate-identity REFACTOR test; neutering `CanonicalDigest` failed GOLDEN, MUTATION and SECURITY; renaming the real YAML's `slice_id` failed CONFORMANCE naming the mismatch in both directions; and changing the CLI's violation label failed its report test. One planned mutation was reported as **not useful and replaced**: disabling the violations exit-code branch was masked by the signature and release-block branches also returning non-zero, so it isolated nothing, and a print-label mutation was substituted that did. `FuzzTodo_THREAT_001` seeds ten cases and asserts `Validate` and `ReleaseDecision` never panic on malformed enum and free-text fields; a 10s run executed roughly 41,000 inputs, found 82 new interesting ones and zero failures, so no crashers were persisted under `testdata/fuzz` and the corpus remains the ten seeds in the test file

branch main. **RED reproduced live before the change** at 1440x900 on `/workspace/app/people`: three scroll regions were configured ad hoc and disagreed with each other. `.main-scroll` computed `scrollbar-width: auto` with `scrollbar-color: auto` -- a 15px native bar -- against `.primary-nav` and `.data-table-scroll` both using `thin` plus a themed token, and it carried no `role`, no `tabindex` and no accessible name at all while scrolling 466px, so a keyboard user could not reach it. `.action-launcher-dialog` was a fourth untokenized region. **Verified live after the change**, rebuilding the wasm bundle then the server binary in that order: all five regions now render through one `ScrollRegion` component and agree -- `.main-scroll` at `thin` with a themed `scrollbar-color`, `tabindex="0"` and an accessible name resolved through `aria-labelledby` to the page heading; `.primary-nav` (`Main`), `.sidebar` (`Workspace navigation`) and `.data-table-scroll` (`Authorized people`) all `thin`, tokenized and focusable; `.action-launcher-dialog` tokenized and named `Go to`, deliberately not focusable itself because focus belongs on its input under the standard ARIA dialog pattern. **UXAUDIT-008's matched pair survived the consolidation**, which was the main regression risk: `.data-table-scroll` still computes `max-height: 738px` together with `overflow-y: auto` in the same context, its `th` still `sticky`, 20 rows rendered -- the pairing whose split clipped 16 workers unreachably earlier the same day, and the rule-level invariant test still guards it. Three RED clauses did not reproduce and were deliberately left alone rather than rebuilt: scroll chaining is already prevented because all regions compute `overscroll-behavior: contain`; `html` and `body` both compute `overflow: hidden`, so popovers cannot create accidental body scroll; and sticky headers do not detach, proven in UXAUDIT-008 by 0px column drift across all six columns scrolled fully right and 200px down. `.main-scroll` keeps `overflow-x: hidden` as a deliberate decision -- every region beneath it that can need horizontal scroll owns its own, and a regression test pins `.data-table-scroll` keeping horizontal overflow so wide content cannot be stranded by the shell's hidden axis. All five tests were mutation-verified against a real break and observed failing before restore: removing `scrollbar-width` from the new `.main-scroll` rule failed the PRIMARY naming the missing token; setting `Focusable: false` on `.main-scroll` failed the BROWSER with `page region ... is not keyboard-focusable`; removing the `Aria` map from `.sidebar` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `element has no accessible name`; rendering a duplicate region with the same id failed the PERFORMANCE with `id="data-table-scroll" occurrences = 2, want exactly 1`; and reintroducing UXAUDIT-008's exact broken pairing failed the REGRESSION with the same message its own historical comment records. **Boundaries, named rather than glossed.** A shared `scroll-region` marker class was deliberately not added to the DOM -- a first attempt broke roughly eight pre-existing tests that assert exact `class=` values -- so the five regions are reached through one comma-joined selector list built from an exported `ScrollRegionSelectors` list instead, keeping the single source of truth in Go without changing rendered markup. Scroll-edge shadows are scoped only to `.data-table-scroll`, which is already `position: relative`; adding `position: relative` blind to the other four risked changing the containing block for an unaudited absolutely-positioned descendant. The shell itself owns no `ScrollRegion` because its contract is to declare no scroll of its own and defer to the five, which an existing test already pins. `scroll_restoration_wasm_test.go` compiles under `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm` but this repository's CI never executes wasm tests, so only its compilation is proven. Two golden shell digests were re-pinned for the new `tabindex`/`id` attributes after diffing the rendered markup and confirming only the intended attributes changed

title: Replace the mobile sidebar with a viewport-safe application shell
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: at 390 px or 320 px the expanded navigation consumes the content viewport, collapsed navigation still constrains the page, the header wraps unpredictably, or navigation and content create competing page-level scroll regions
green: narrow viewports use an accessible overlay drawer with focus containment and restoration, the compact header retains the page identity and essential actions, the content owns one vertical scroll surface, and expanded/collapsed state does not change content width after the transition completes
refactor: one responsive shell and one navigation model serve desktop and mobile; do not fork page implementations by viewport
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Performance` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit001_shell_drawer_test.go`), with the focus trap itself in `drawer_focus_wasm.go` / `drawer_focus_native.go` and its own js/wasm-tagged test, plus `tools/uxqual/browser/uxaudit001_mobile_shell.spec.mjs`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%, `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server at 320x720, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order (the assets are `go:embed`ed, so the reverse order silently serves a stale UI). Measured against the audit's own numbers: the header is a single 81px row where it had wrapped to 134px; `main` starts at y=81, 11% of the viewport, where it had started at y=451, 63%; visible content height is 639px where it was 269px; and there is exactly one page-level scroll region, `MAIN.main-scroll`, where there had been two competing ones. No horizontal overflow at 320px, which was already correct and is not regressed. Opening the drawer leaves content width unchanged at 320px. The drawer itself was verified open on screen: `left` 0px, `visibility` visible, bounding rect left 0, backdrop `display` block, `aria-expanded` true, `role=dialog`, `aria-modal=true` and the accessible name `Workspace navigation` present only while open; an Escape keydown closes it and returns `aria-expanded` to false. Two defects were found by that live run and fixed, neither visible to the Go suite as it then stood. The drawer's open rule matched the element and sat later in the cascade at higher specificity with no `!important` on either side, yet never applied -- the sidebar stayed at `left:-336px` and `visibility:hidden` whether the class was present or not. And the backdrop could never appear at all, because `.nav-drawer-backdrop` sets `display:none` while its open rule set background, inset, position and z-index but never `display`. Both are now `!important`-guarded, matching this package's existing idiom for breakpoint overrides, and the compound per-property `transition` shorthand the browser was mis-parsing was simplified to a single declaration. The test that would have caught them was added rather than the fix merely being applied: the suite previously substring-matched stylesheet text, which proves a rule exists but not that it wins the cascade, so `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_001` now parses a rule's declaration body into a property map and requires the open rule to restate `inset-inline-start` and `visibility` with a different value and an `!important` priority, and the backdrop's open rule to set `display` to something other than `none`. Verified failable by reverting each fix independently. REFACTOR's one-shell clause holds: `NavigationDrawerScope` shares a single `ui.UseState` flag between the header trigger and the sidebar, there is no per-viewport fork, and the tests assert exactly one `#workspace-navigation` and one `.primary-nav` across five pages. **Boundary.** Focus containment and restoration could not be verified in the browser pane and are not claimed here: calling `.focus()` on a real visible input among the drawer's 32 focusable descendants leaves `document.activeElement` at BODY, so neither focus entering the dialog nor returning to the trigger is observable in that environment. The trap is covered by a js/wasm-tagged unit test that compiles and by the Playwright spec, neither of which was executed here; the Escape-to-close half of the keyboard contract was confirmed live because it does not depend on focus

title: Make the global launcher perform actions rather than duplicate navigation
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: `Start an action` contains only links to Journeys and People, stays open after focus leaves, or lists actions the viewer cannot execute
green: the launcher lists ranked authorized actions such as Promote worker, explains disabled actions without disclosure, supports keyboard search and dismissal on Escape/outside focus, and uses a navigation label instead of an action label when only destinations are available

evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_003` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_003_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_003_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_003_Security` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_003_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit003_action_launcher_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean including under `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. RED was reproduced live before any change: clicking `Start an action` opened a popover holding exactly two entries, both plain navigation links to `/workspace/app/journeys` and `/workspace/app/people`, and pressing Escape left the trigger's `aria-expanded` at `true`. **Verified live against the running server after the change, as this section's preamble requires**, having rebuilt the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. The launcher now offers six real actions rather than destinations -- `Start Promotion for Isaac`, `Wesley`, `Peter`, `Khadija`, `Dominic` and `Linh`, each carrying `mode=new&worker=<id>` -- and the trigger keeps its action label because actions genuinely exist for this viewer. Dismissal was proven live on all three paths the Go tests could not execute: an Escape keydown dispatched at the panel closes it, moving `aria-expanded` from `true` to `false` and returning `document.activeElement` to the trigger, and an outside pointerdown closes it likewise. The no-disclosure clause is proven by value rather than by flag, following the pattern PROMOUX-001 and PROMOUX-004 established: a create-unauthorized viewer receives byte-identical reason text across eligible, ineligible, active-conflict and zero-value workers, and the rendered markup carries the generic withheld string while never containing `workflow.promotion_active_conflict` or `workflow.no_promotion_path`; an authorized viewer, by contrast, sees genuinely different reasons. When a viewer has no authorized actions the control relabels itself through `action_launcher.navigate_trigger` -- `Go to`, `Gehe zu`, and the Arabic equivalent -- derived live from the resolved items by `actionLauncherIsNavigationOnly` rather than carried as a separate prop that could drift from reality, which is what GREEN asks for instead of fabricating an action to fill the menu. A real disclosure regression was caught and fixed during implementation rather than shipped: the first pass rendered every admitted worker's name unconditionally into the launcher's server markup, hidden but present, which broke roughly seven unrelated page-scoped tests by leaking names across surfaces. It was corrected by sourcing from `admittedPeople(view)` and gating the results panel on the open state, the same pattern `GlobalSearch` already uses. **Boundaries.** No formal semantic-action registry type exists in this codebase; rather than invent one, the shared resolution step was extracted as `personWorkflowActions` so the People directory rows and the launcher call the same function instead of the launcher hand-rolling its own list. `page_person.go` and `global_search.go` keep their own independent copies of similar logic -- pre-existing duplication, found and left alone. The DOM Escape behaviour lives in a `js && wasm` file that this repository's CI never executes either, so the lane could only compile and link it; the live run recorded above is what actually proves it. Three whole-shell goldens were re-pinned after the new closed-launcher markup was dumped and read, not merely observed to differ

title: Render reporting lines as a coherent, navigable ownership tree
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: reporting lines appear as disconnected cards, visual nesting disagrees with manager edges, a worker appears outside the visible root without an explanation, or keyboard users cannot traverse the hierarchy
green: connectors, indentation, expand/collapse state, manager summaries and orphan/withheld explanations reflect the authorized server projection exactly; flat and tree modes preserve selection and expose equivalent information to assistive technology
refactor: the flat organization list, organization tree and Myself subtree consume one organization-node component and one authorized relationship projection
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Property` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit004_organization_tree_test.go`), and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Integration` in `internal/data/orgfacts` (`reader_test.go`, against real PostgreSQL via pgtest); new `internal/humanwork/productui/organization_relationships.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 75.9% (`internal/data/orgfacts`) and 84.9% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean including under `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm`, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The root cause was worse than the todo's wording suggests and was found by reading rather than assumed: the tree nested by **matching `Person.Manager` display-name text**, so two people sharing a name collapsed together and a rename silently rebuilt the hierarchy. Nesting now derives from `org.ResolveManagerRelationships`, the authorized projection PROMOUX-005 built, keyed on a new `Person.ManagerID` carrying the manager's raw worker id, with `internal/data/orgfacts` supplying the facts and `tools/uxqual/productclient` wiring the id from the wire's `ManagerRef`. Agreement between visual nesting and manager edges is proven generically rather than by example, because a renderer that indents by array order passes any hand-built tree: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_004_Property` generates 200 seeded random populations and requires every nested node's parent to equal ground truth, every worker to appear exactly once, and any ground-truth manager absent from the population to produce a non-empty explanation rather than a silent root. Hierarchy is never invented. A manager outside the visible population, a withheld relationship and a reporting-line cycle -- the last detected by a Tarjan-style depth-first pass in `breakOwnershipCycles` -- each render as a root at level one carrying a distinct localized explanation, never reparented under something else and never dropped. `organizationPlacementFor` maps every `org.ResolutionStatus` and `people.Disclosure` exhaustively, proven by a subtest that iterates the full status set, and its zero value -- an unresolved relationship -- is required to be non-nested with an explanation, so a node whose relationship never resolved cannot become a false root of the visible tree. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Before the change the reporting-lines view exposed **no tree semantics at all** -- zero `role="tree"`, zero `role="treeitem"`, zero `aria-level`, with five `aria-expanded` nodes -- so assistive technology saw disclosure widgets rather than a hierarchy. After it, `/workspace/app/organization?org_view=tree` renders one `role="tree"`, **64 `role="treeitem"` nodes** and 19 `role="group"` wrappers, and every one of those 64 nodes' declared `aria-level` was checked against an independently counted DOM ancestor depth with **zero mismatches**, at real depths of one through four. REFACTOR is satisfied by one `organizationPersonCard` component serving the flat list, the tree and the Myself subtree, the last of which now shows the viewer and their own reports re-rooted to level one rather than the whole company. Two pre-existing tests were rewritten with UUID-based fixtures because their assertions encoded the defect -- `TestOrganizationReportingDisclosuresAndAmbiguousNames` and `TestOwnershipTreeDoesNotDropCyclesOrOrphans` required `role="tree"` and `role="treeitem"` to be absent -- and `TestMyselfPageUsesOnlyTheAuthenticatedViewerBinding` moved from `role="list"` to `role="tree"`. **Boundaries.** `ManagerRelationshipWithheld` is wired end to end but no production caller sets it true yet. The AMBIGUOUS, STALE and DISAGREEING statuses are unreachable from today's one-manager-per-worker population, so they are tested by direct construction rather than through the adapter. Keyboard traversal is Tab-based over real links and buttons rather than full roving-tabindex arrow-key APG behaviour. The Browser and Accessibility tests are static SSR and DOM parses following this package's precedent; the live run recorded above is what proves the rendered tree semantics

title: Replace implementation vocabulary with task-oriented product language
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation

green: every page, empty state, loading state and error uses concise task language, gives a clear next step, and keeps technical identifiers behind an explicit diagnostics disclosure for authorized operators
refactor: centralize copy keys in the locale catalog; do not scatter replacement strings through renderers
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006_Golden`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006_I18N` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit006_vocabulary_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 61.7% (`internal/humanwork/workspace`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception) and 84.8% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED -- including this repo's frontend i18n gate, which would fail on a missing locale key -- on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. The durable artifact is a vocabulary guard rather than a list of individual string fixes, because without one the next subtitle to mention a worker projection reintroduces the defect silently. `uxaudit006BannedVocabulary` is a named, documented slice holding `JourneyService`, `ListWorkers`, `gRPC`, `authenticated cell`, `live cell`, `server-enforced boundary`, `tenant appearance`, `credential role fallback`, `worker projection` and `governed journey service`; `uxaudit006ScanVocabulary` scans the full rendered document case-insensitively, and the PRIMARY renders every `PageDefinitions()` entry in all three locales plus the Admin home under four role sets and fails on any match. The guard proves itself non-vacuous by first scanning a deliberately seeded banned string and requiring a non-empty result. Copy was corrected in en-US, de-DE and ar rather than English alone, since a German sentence containing `JourneyService` is still a violation: `page.people.subtitle`, `page.organization.subtitle`, `organization.metadata_boundary`, `organization.empty_title` and `empty_description`, `shell.authenticated_scope`, `shell.loading_authorized`, `admin.journeys_unavailable_reason`, `admin.studio_unavailable_reason`, `roles.assignments_help`, `organization_visibility.boundary_title` and `boundary_detail`, and `appearance.tenant`. REFACTOR is satisfied by moving hardcoded strings into the catalog rather than rewording them in place: `page_admin.go`'s `LIVE CELL`, `authenticated cell` and `canonical gRPC service` literals and `page_insights.go`'s not-available-in-this-cell literal became `admin.hero_eyebrow`, `admin.hero_description`, `admin.journey_card_description`, `admin.studio_card_description` and `insights.attention_description`. `model.go`'s `View.Source` moved from `JourneyService` to `Workforce directory`, which is the single value feeding both the footer and the Settings page's data source fact, so one change cleared both surfaces. GREEN's next-step requirement is met where it was missing: the Organization empty state now tells the reader to ask an administrator to check their access, and the Admin journeys-unavailable reason tells them to refresh. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Nine pages -- home, people, organization, insights, admin, roles, settings, work and journeys -- were fetched from the running server with script and style elements stripped, and every one is clean of the banned vocabulary in visible text. The footer that previously read `Live source · JourneyService` now reads `Live source · Workforce directory`. The only remaining occurrence of any banned term anywhere in the served documents is `grpc` inside the `journey-config` JSON island's WebSocket tunnel URL, `ws://127.0.0.1:8080/workspace/grpc`, which is a transport endpoint rather than user-facing copy. UXAUDIT-007 is not regressed: the acting-context strings remain absent. The lane found one leftover during its sweep and left it because `Routes()` is consumed only by a test rather than served: its discovery-document description still read `backed by canonical JourneyService RPCs`. That was corrected during review rather than carried, since a description that is ever exposed would leak the same vocabulary. **Boundary.** `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_006_Browser` is a static SSR/DOM assertion parsing the rendered document, not a live-browser check; the live confirmation above was performed separately by the reviewer against the running server

title: Scope acting-context notices to situations that change user authority
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: a `Compensation Review` or `Acting as yourself` badge appears globally on unrelated pages, looks clickable without an action, or competes with the page title
green: the shell shows a persistent banner only for delegated, view-as, elevated or break-glass authority; ordinary self context is quiet; task-specific review context appears inside the affected workflow with a clear explanation and exit action
refactor: one acting-context component renders server-resolved authority state across all pages
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007_Security` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit007_acting_context_test.go`), plus `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_007_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/workspace` (`product_shell_test.go`), `TestChromePairsPurposeWithItsLogoutHref` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` and `TestPrincipalChipPairsPurposeWithItsExit` in `tools/uxqual/render/journey`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.3% (`internal/humanwork/productui`), 61.7% (`internal/humanwork/workspace`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised by this change), 100.0% (`tools/uxqual/render/workspace`), 97.0% (`tools/uxqual/render/journey`), 86.1% (`tools/uxqual/journeyclient`) and 84.8% (`tools/uxqual/productclient`); `go build ./...` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Signed in as an ordinary self-context user, `/workspace/app/home` no longer renders `Acting as yourself` or `Compensation Review` anywhere, its header reduced to `H Human Capital Management Suite` with the navigation, search, locale and avatar controls and no banner; `/workspace/app/journeys` is likewise clean, its only remaining occurrence of the purpose being inside the hidden JSON config island that transports it to the client. On `/workspace/journey`, the affected workflow, the purpose renders with its explanation as `Purpose: compensation_review` beside an exit control reading `Exit compensation_review and sign out` that points at `/workspace/logout` and carries the same `aria-label`. The RED had two independent sources and both are closed. `header_identity.go` rendered a hardcoded `identity.ActingLabel` on every page with no dependency on any authority projection, and `ActingAuthorityBanner` bannered for any valid authority context including plain own authority. Acting-context notices now come from one component, satisfying REFACTOR. The disclosure rule is deliberately inverted from this repository's usual fail-closed convention, and tested as such: `AuthorityState.noticeworthy()` is exhaustive with no permissive default, and every unrecognised value -- proven with `AuthorityState("quantum_delegation_v2")` in both packages -- discloses rather than suppresses, because silently hiding a banner would tell a user acting under delegated or break-glass authority that they are acting as themselves, which is the more dangerous error. Only ordinary self context is quiet. The second half of the defect was data wiring rather than rendering: `config.Purpose`, an admitted principal's authorized data-processing purpose, was being passed as the shell's generic authorized scope by `internal/humanwork/workspace/product_shell.go` and as `Session.Scope` by `tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/product_wasm.go`. Both now stop, and `Session.Scope` carries a doc comment pinning its contract against a repeat. The exit action was found missing by the live run after the first fix landed: `chrome()` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient/projector.go` built the masthead's `Principal` with Subject, Roles and Purpose but never `LogoutHref`, even though `render/journey`'s `principalChip` already knew how to render one. Both are fixed, the control names what it exits rather than reading as a bare Sign out, and the tests assert the pairing by value -- purpose and its exit destination together -- because asserting either half alone is exactly what let the gap through

title: Give the People directory one stable, high-density table viewport
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: the page and table compete for vertical scrolling, sticky headers detach from their columns, sorting jumps the page, only a few rows fit in a desktop viewport, or every row repeats a large unavailable-workflow message
green: filters and results share a stable layout, only the data region updates on sort/filter/page-size changes, headers remain aligned and sticky, density is usable at 100 rows, scroll position is preserved, and compact row actions communicate availability without visual noise
refactor: use the reusable configurable data-table component and server-persisted table preferences; no People-only sorting or pagination implementation
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008_Performance`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008_Regression` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_008_DirectoryTableModeRestoration` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit008_people_table_test.go`), plus `TestPeopleDirectoryOnlyRouteChangeCoversEveryDirectoryFilter` in `tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm` (`product_focus_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 93.4% (`internal/humanwork/productui`); `go build ./...` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. The RED had three independent sources and the fix took two passes, the second driven by a regression the first pass introduced. (1) Sticky headers detached because CSS `position` never inherits: the pre-existing rules stuck `<thead>` and the header `<tr>` but never the `<th>`, so the header cells' own computed `position` stayed `static` -- measured as such at 1024x768 before the fix, and `sticky` after. (2) Only a few rows fit a desktop viewport because `dataTableStylesStylesheet`'s shared `@media (max-width:1050px)` card mode caught 1024px, stacking each worker into a 199px `display:grid` card; the People directory now keeps the real 63px-row table down to 761px through `.people-directory`-scoped counter-rules that restate the shared component's own above-1050px values, leaving History and Organization on the shared breakpoint untouched. (3) The first pass scoped a taller `max-height` cap unconditionally; because `.people-directory .data-table-scroll` is two classes it beat the card-mode reset's `max-height:none` even inside that media query, but it did not restate `overflow`, leaving a bounded box still declared `overflow:visible` inside a `section.surface` that clips -- the live re-audit found 16 of 20 workers (Anika HC-21013, Aya HC-21033 and 14 more) rendering below the clipping edge and unreachable at the page's maximum scroll, a defect the first pass created and no test caught. A bounded `max-height` and a scrolling `overflow` are a matched pair; the cap now lives inside its own `min-width:761px` context with `overflow:auto` in the same rule, so the pair can never be split across contexts again, and the `scroll wrapper max-height and overflow stay a matched pair` subtest encodes that as a rule-level invariant rather than a substring grep -- mutation-verified against the exact broken pairing, which it failed with `found a bounded max-height with no scrolling overflow in the same block` and passed on revert. Live sweep at 375, 760, 900, 1024, 1440 and 1920px: every row reachable at every width, no clipping anywhere; card mode below 761px keeps `max-height:none`/`overflow:visible`. At 1024x768 the directory now shows 9 of 20 rows fully visible against 0 at the original audit, with the sticky header holding at the scroll region's top edge and all six columns aligned to 0px drift even when scrolled fully right and 200px down; 161px of horizontal scroll inside the region is the deliberate cost of keeping real columns rather than cards. 1440x900 is preserved at 11 of 20 rows with no horizontal scroll, and 1920x1080 shows 13. PROMOUX-001's server-provided unavailability reason was not deleted or reworded to win the density -- `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001` and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_001_Security` pass unmodified, the full text surviving in `title` and an `sr-only` span referenced by `aria-describedby` while the visible layout carries a compact `.people-availability-badge`. A real latent defect surfaced on the way: `eligible` was missing from `peopleDirectoryOnlyRouteChange`'s mutable-key set, so toggling the promotion-eligible filter triggered a full page reload instead of a directory-only refresh; it is now in the set and covered

title: Remove unavailable Experience Studio from primary navigation
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: Experience Studio remains a first-class menu item for a role or release where no usable authorized inventory or authoring capability exists
green: the destination is omitted until the registry reports an admitted capability; an authorized preview, when intentionally enabled, is labeled Preview, explains its limitations and cannot publish or mutate outside its gate
refactor: navigation availability derives from the page registry and release gate, not a route-name exception
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011_Security` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011_Conformance` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit011_studio_admission_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. REFACTOR forbids a route-name exception, so the fix is a registry field rather than a special case: `PageDefinition.Admitted bool`, whose zero value is false, gates both navigation-building loops through `navigationPrimaryEligible` and `navigationChildEligible`. Studio's registry row is otherwise untouched -- it keeps `ParentNav: PageAdmin` exactly as before -- and navigation code names no specific route anywhere. The mechanism was verified by reverting only the `Admitted` checks and confirming all four tests fail with their expected RED messages, then restoring and confirming green. `validateAuthorizedNavigationItem` also requires `Admitted`, so a server answer claiming `Authorized: true` for an unadmitted page cannot smuggle it back into the menu. The default is not-navigable rather than navigable, which matters because the opposite default silently readmits every future unbuilt page and is how this defect arose: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_011_Conformance` builds a synthetic definition with `Admitted` left at its zero value, asserts both predicates reject it, then flips it true and asserts acceptance, independent of the live registry's contents. Sixteen genuinely implemented pages were marked admitted, identified by the absence of the not-published-to-this-UI stub pattern the other pages carry. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. The primary navigation went from 14 destinations to 13; the only removal is `/workspace/app/studio`, nothing was added, and all thirteen other baseline destinations remain -- home, myself, journeys, work, history, people, organization, insights, admin, admin/worker-ids, admin/roles, admin/organization-visibility and appearance. Omission from the menu is not authorization: `/workspace/app/studio` still answers 200 with its existing explanatory unavailable state for an authorized role, and `internal/humanwork/workspace/product_shell.go` still refuses unauthorized roles through `PageVisible` independently of `Admitted`, so the change moves nothing across that boundary in either direction. The rule generalized rather than special-casing one page, which was the point of forbidding a route exception: eleven further registry entries backed by no real service -- Policy Studio, Policy simulation, Configuration center, Integration operations, Reconciliation workbench, Privacy telemetry, Performance budgets, Browser matrix, Assistive tech, Disaster recovery and Release gate -- are now excluded by the same predicate, proven generically in the Conformance test rather than by name. Those had not appeared in the live baseline only because the running binary predated their addition to source. Those four WEB contracts are about their named tests returning deterministic authorization-filtered results, not about navigation placement, so inverting the nav assertion does not weaken them. **Boundaries.** GREEN's optional labeled Preview mode was not built; no code path enables it, which is consistent with its off-by-default requirement. `tools/uxqual/pagedef`, named in the Refs, has no dependency on `productui` and was left untouched

title: Eliminate layout shifts during server-backed loading and navigation
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: route changes remount the shell, server fetches collapse or expand major page regions, loading proxies do not preserve final geometry, or focus and scroll jump when data resolves
green: software navigation retains shell and page chrome, each asynchronous region owns a size-compatible skeleton or inline progress state, only affected regions update, focus and scroll remain stable, and cumulative layout shift stays within the declared frontend budget
refactor: one async-region state model covers loading, empty, stale, failure and resolved states across components
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Performance`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Fault` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Regression` in `internal/humanwork/productui` (`uxaudit012_layout_shift_test.go`); new `async_region.go` and `layout_shift.go`; no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover ./internal/humanwork/productui/` PASS at 93.3%; `go build ./...` clean, `GOOS=js GOARCH=wasm go build ./tools/uxqual/cmd/journeywasm/` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. No pre-existing test was renamed or altered. RED's sharpest clause -- loading proxies do not preserve final geometry -- was literally true rather than hypothetical, and three real defects were found by measuring rather than inspecting. `.loading-row` declared `min-height:76px` against `.work-row`'s 86px, a ten-pixel shift per row on every Home, Work and Journeys cold load; `.loading-table-row` declared 67px against `.people-row`'s 65px; and `.loading-table-head` declared 46px against `.people-columns`' 44px, both on every People and History cold load. All three are aligned in `typed_mig_C.go` with comments naming the guarding test. The geometry proof compares dimensions rather than asserting a skeleton exists, which is the distinction that makes it a test of this clause at all: the PRIMARY parses the built stylesheet with an exact standalone-selector matcher -- so a density variant such as `:root[data-hcm-density="compact"] .work-row` cannot be mistaken for the base rule -- and requires each proxy and its resolved counterpart to declare identical `min-height`. It was verified against the pre-fix values and failed there. REFACTOR's single model is `AsyncRegionState` with exactly the five states named -- Loading, Empty, Stale, Failure, Resolved -- as an int enum whose **zero value is Loading, not Resolved**. That direction is the load-bearing one here: a region descriptor that forgets to set its state renders through the sized skeleton rather than as a false-resolved empty box, which is precisely the shift. `UsesGeometryProxy` and `Announcement` switch over all five members with no default branch, returning `ErrUnknownAsyncRegionState` for anything outside the set. The fault clause is proven stronger than size compatibility: `BuildFailure` renders through the same `loadingProxyBody` call as the loading builders, and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_012_Fault` requires the loading and failure bodies to be **byte-identical** for People, Work and Organization, so a region cannot collapse when its fetch fails. The Performance entry asserts a deterministic shift score (`|delta height| / viewport height`) rather than elapsed wall-clock time, deliberately avoiding this machine's unreliable timing, and separately proves the check rejects a real violation. **Verified live against the running server, as this section's preamble requires**, after rebuilding the wasm bundle and then the server binary in that order. Cumulative layout shift measured through a `PerformanceObserver` on `layout-shift` entries with `buffered: true`, excluding entries with recent input: `/workspace/app/people` resolved **20 rendered rows with CLS 0.00000 and zero shift entries** -- a real skeleton-to-content transition rather than a trivially empty page -- and `/workspace/app/work` likewise measured zero. Software navigation was tested by clicking a real navigation link from People to Organization: the `.app-shell` and `nav.primary-nav` elements are the **same DOM nodes** before and after, disproving RED's remount clause directly, with CLS 0.00000 across the transition. **Boundaries.** No governed numeric CLS budget exists anywhere in the repository -- `page_performance_budgets.go` is an honest stub that refuses to invent one until a governed service publishes -- so `AsyncRegionLayoutShiftBudget = 0.1` is declared as an engineering threshold, documented as not business-authoritative, in the same category as `latencygate`'s hardcoded p95 figures. The Organization and Insights loading families were not individually re-verified pixel-for-pixel; only the People, Work and History row families were fixed and proven. `BuildFailure` and `BuildAsyncRegion` are tested primitives not yet wired into the live wasm router's fetch-error path. History's resolved row has no declared `min-height`, being content-driven, so its parity with the shared proxy could not be proven pixel-exact the way People's could. The pre-existing `appShellWithHeading` LoadError branch was deliberately left alone as a different working contract

title: Keep login persona promises consistent with usable capabilities
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: a sample persona description promises payroll, recruiting or management work that is absent after login, or different personas land on indistinguishable menus despite different effective roles
green: each development persona names only admitted capabilities, is bound to a real visible worker where required, lands on a role-appropriate home, and has browser tests that prove both visible and denied page/action differences
refactor: persona copy and expected navigation derive from the same fixture and effective-capability projection
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014` (the PRIMARY named in the TEST field), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_Security`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_Regression` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_CopyMatchesMenu` in `internal/humanwork/workspace` (`todo_uxaudit_014_test.go`), `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_Integration` in `test/workspace` (`todo_uxaudit_014_test.go`, against a real Postgres-backed `roleaccessstore.Store`), `TestComposeDevPersonasAccessAndPurposeMatchRoleBundle` in `internal/application` (`dev_personas_test.go`) and the rewritten `TestUXBLIND005PersonaCopyNamesUsefulTasks` in `internal/humanwork/workspace` (`uxblind_login_test.go`); no migration required. `go test -count=1 -cover` PASS at 62.8% (`internal/humanwork/workspace`, under its recorded `below_floor` exception and raised by this change) and 81.3% (`internal/application`); `go build ./...` clean, `go vet` clean, gofmt clean, staticcheck clean and `go run ./tools/quality` PASSED on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3); branch main. **Verified live against the running server**, signing in as all four personas by real form POST and decoding each issued token. Both RED clauses reproduced before the fix and are closed after it. Clause 2 was literal: `hiring-manager` and `payroll-manager` rendered byte-identical destination sets despite disjoint role bundles, because `productui.PageVisible` and `roleaccess.DefaultPagePermissions` both sort `manager`, `hr_partner`, `hiring_manager` and `payroll_manager` into one bucket -- only three distinguishable authorization shapes exist for four persona slots, so one collision is unavoidable without admitting a real payroll surface. Clause 1 was the copy: `loginPersonaDescription` was a hand-written `switch` on persona ID promising `Review payroll information, reports` and `Review hiring and organization requests` while no payroll or recruiting destination is admitted anywhere (`PagePayBenefitRecon`, `PageHeadcount`, `PageRequisition` and `PageCandidates` all leave `Admitted` at its zero value). The fix took three passes because each one left a smaller version of the same promise standing. First the description was made derived rather than written, and `payroll-manager`'s bundle narrowed to `worker_self`. That left the card still headed `Payroll manager` and the credential still stamped `purpose: payroll_processing` -- naming a role the token did not carry and a processing purpose `authz.PolicyTable` grants only to `comp_admin`; both now derive from the worker's own record and the role bundle (`Finance Director (self-service)`, `self_service_view`), and the two `worker_self` personas are distinguished by real data rather than prose. The third pass closed REFACTOR itself: the derived copy read `productui`'s registry admission while the menu and the route both read `roleaccess`, and the two disagreed -- `worker_self` reaches Insights under roleaccess but not under the registry, so the card understated by one destination. `product_shell.go` overrides the registry result with `roleaccess.CanPageAction` whenever page permissions are configured, and `roleaccessstore.Store.Bootstrap` always configures them, so roleaccess is what a live server enforces and is now the single projection the copy derives from. `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_014_CopyMatchesMenu` pins the agreement by set equality against a real signed-in `GET /workspace/app/home`, folding group labels through `ParentNav` rather than special-casing names, and was mutation-verified: reverting to `PageVisible` failed it with `symmetric difference: [Insights]` for both `worker_self` personas. `_Regression` and `_Security` were mutation-verified too -- restoring the `payroll_manager` bundle failed the first with `render identical destinations`, and forcing `allowed := true` in `serveProduct` failed the second across ten subtests. Live route checks confirm authorization is enforced at the route, not merely hidden from the menu: as `worker_self`, `/people`, `/journeys`, `/work`, `/history`, `/admin` and `/admin/roles` all return 403 while `/insights`, `/myself` and `/organization` return 200, matching its card exactly; `hiring-manager` reaches `/people` at 200 and is refused `/admin` at 403. `insights` was removed from `_Security`'s denied-route list as part of the third pass -- not to make a test pass, but because the live server genuinely admits it for `worker_self`; five denied routes remain and still prove real refusal. **Commit blocker resolved 2026-09-13:** this close-out was parked because `test/workspace` was already red at HEAD -- `TestPromotionWorkspaceRendersFromTheLiveCellWithZeroEffects` (CSP subtest) and `TestTodo_UX_004_Browser` still asserted the `uxqual.wasm` enhancement (a `script-src` hash, `wasm-unsafe-eval`, the contract island and `PathWasm`) that 60ca21b9 deliberately withholds in `internal/humanwork/workspace/assets.go` because that bundle rebuilt the request form without CSRF, worker, locale and form-owner binding. The refusal is the security-correct behaviour and the internal `assets_test.go` already pins it, so the two tests now branch on `workspace.BundleBuilt()` like the rest of `test/workspace`: a build carrying the bundle keeps every enhanced assertion, and the native-only build must send `script-src 'none'` and serve no `<script>` or `PathWasm` reference -- stricter than before, not looser; `go test -count=1 ./test/workspace/` PASS. The Refs link to the non-existent `specs/trusted-request-boundary.md` now points at the `Trusted request boundary` section of `specs/http-grpc-endpoint-contract.md`. Recorded consequence for PROMOUX-015: `hc-054-thomas-baker` is the routed ASSIGNEE_ONLY finance approver in the demo tenant but this persona now carries `worker_self`, which reaches no My Work, so a real finance-approver role bundle is needed before a multi-persona journey can act as him

title: Differentiate Journeys from My Work by user task
section: 69. Live product UX audit remediation
red: Journeys and My Work render nearly identical lists and empty states, or My Work fails to emphasize assignments, due dates, ownership and the next executable action
green: My Work is an action queue ordered by urgency and ownership; Journeys is a lifecycle tracker grouped by subject and status; both deep-link to the same canonical intent workspace and retain filters on return
refactor: share journey summaries, status dimensions and list primitives while keeping page composition task-specific
evidence: `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017` (PRIMARY) in `internal/humanwork/productui`, `tools/uxqual/productclient`, `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` and `tools/uxqual/render/journey`; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Regression` in the same four; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Accessibility`, `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Browser` and `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths` in `internal/humanwork/productui`; `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Integration` and `TestTodo_UXAUDIT_017_Security` (embedded PostgreSQL) in `internal/application`; `TestJourneyWorkItemSummarySecurity` and `TestAssigneeNameResolverIsExactMemoizedAndBounded` in `internal/intent/app`; `TestJourneyWorkItemSummaryReachesTheWire` in `internal/transport/journey`; `TestStageStatusDimensionTable` and `TestNextStepLabelVocabulary` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient`; no migration. `go test -count=1` PASS for productui (93.4%), productclient (85.4%), journeyclient (84.3%), render/journey (96.5%), transport/journey (80.4%) and humanwork/workspace, re-run by the orchestrator; `go build ./...` and js/wasm `go vet` clean; `go run ./tools/policy/apigate/cmd/apigate -root .` PASS with no endpoint-manifest change (Go 1.26.3, windows/arm64); branch main. **Contract:** `Journey.current_work_item` (field 20, `JourneyWorkItemSummary`) carries the current work item's kind, status, assignee principal id and display name, `due_at`, the viewer's permitted actions and membership, with no work item id because raw ids stay diagnostics-only under PROMOUX-008. The orchestrator chose this over opening `WorkService` to the browser, which would have widened `journeyclient/rpc_adapter.go`'s deliberate JourneyService-only allowlist. `internal/intent/app/journey_work_summary.go` builds it from the work items the list already loads (no added reads) and discloses nothing unless `workitem.Visible` admits the viewer; the assignee additionally requires `workitem.ContextVisible`, actions are exactly `workitem.PermittedActions`, and display names resolve only by exact worker id or key, memoized and capped at 16 principals per page. The real-database Security test proves an ASSIGNEE_ONLY approval discloses no summary to its author or an outsider. **My Work** is an action queue ordered by urgency tier (repair, then blocked or awaiting approval, then waiting, then terminal), then the viewer's standing on the current work item (holds, may claim, others), then stage-derived person-versus-workflow ownership, then the real due date; rows lead with `Your next action` drawn only from server-granted actions, then the next step, assignment and due date, falling back to the stage-derived next step and waiting-on line plus one honest note when no summary is disclosed. An `Assigned to me` tab (`filter=mine`) scopes to work the viewer holds or may claim; the default view stays all authorized journeys because scoping it would hide a proposer's PROPOSED and BLOCKED journeys, which have no work item. Filter links always carry an explicit `filter=`, fixing a defect where a saved My Work filter could never be cleared. **Journeys** is a lifecycle tracker grouped by subject with each group's statuses and a next step per open card, both pages deep-link to `/workspace/app/journeys?journey=<id>`, and the two empty states differ. **Live verification** on the rebuilt cell (wasm bundle hash matched its manifest): as `hc-054-thomas-baker`, the routed ASSIGNEE_ONLY finance approver, Dominic's and Aya's rows read `Your next action: Claim`, `Assigned to you`, `Due 2026-09-15` and `filter=mine` narrowed seven journeys to those two; as `principal:promotion-approver` and as the admin persona the same rows showed only the stage fallback and note, as the visibility rule requires. **The 390px pass found a defect every HTML-string test missed:** a pre-existing `.work-row .row-main small+small { display:none }` below 1190px hid every row line after the first `<small>`, so on phones, tablets and narrow laptops the queue showed none of the next action, next step, assignment or due date -- and had been silently hiding PROMOUX-003's disposition line too. The orchestrator scoped the rule to a new `row-summary` class so only the grade-change line drops, re-verified at 390px that all facts render with no horizontal scroll, and added `TestWorkRowActionFactsSurviveNarrowWidths`, which fails naming the selector when the positional rule is restored. Mutations verified by name: dropping the ownership or due-date sort keys, `Assigned to me` returning all work, offering a next action without a matching grant (initially survived; the test was tightened), disclosing an assignee without `ContextVisible`, `governed=true`, skipping `Visible`, dropping the wire copy or client projection, removing the name-lookup cap, and restoring the `small+small` rule. Recorded, not fixed: `ListJourneys` already performed one record read per journey and re-simulated unexecuted journeys before this change, so the page is not yet truly batched; the two status vocabularies still differ (`Proposed` versus `Ready to start approval`, and RECORDED is open on Journeys but closed on My Work); the `Awaiting approval` tab matches only its own label, so Manager and Finance approval journeys never appear in it; and in the dev personas the only routed finance approver, Thomas Baker, is the self-service Finance Director persona, which reaches only Myself, Organization and Insights, so signed in through the persona picker he cannot open My Work to act on his own approvals

Earlier work had therefore already fixed the behavior and never written the tests this todo names, so the whole risk here was authoring a suite against behavior that already passes, which passes on its first run by construction and proves nothing. Every one of the six tests was consequently mutation-verified against a real break in production code: dropping the `Keywords` half of `navigationItemFromDefinition` failed the PRIMARY with `NavItem.Keywords = []`; swapping `html.Details`/`html.Summary` for `html.Div` failed the ACCESSIBILITY with `group must be a native
/ disclosure`; weakening `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` from `if ok && allowed[definition.ID]` to `if ok` failed the SECURITY on its zero-grant bundle with `search item "page:help" ... resolves to page "help", which roleaccess denies this role bundle View on`; removing the early exit in `globalSearchScore` moved P95 from roughly 10ms to roughly 30ms past the 20ms budget and failed the PERFORMANCE; making `navigationSearchScore` ignore `item.Keywords` failed the REGRESSION with `alias "dashboard" resolves in menu filtering=false but in global search=true`, and making `BrandLogo` default to a fabricated `harborcare-logo.svg` failed its second pin; dropping `ID: "global-search-input"` from `GlobalSearch` failed the BROWSER naming that exact fragment. The SECURITY test is a property over sixteen role bundles resolved through `roleaccess.DefaultPagePermissions`, `EffectivePagePermissions` and `CanPageAction` rather than through `productui.PageVisible`, because `product_shell.go` overrides the registry fallback with `roleaccess.CanPageAction` whenever page permissions are configured and `roleaccessstore.Store.Bootstrap` always configures them, so the registry is not the authority a live server enforces. It is pinned live: signed in as the `worker_self` persona, searching `adrian` -- a worker outside that viewer's authority -- and `roles` -- the Admin roles page -- both return the empty state, while `organ` returns three authorized results, proving the empty answers are scoping rather than a broken search, and the same persona receives 403 on `/people`, `/journeys`, `/work`, `/history`, `/admin` and `/admin/roles` against 200 on `/insights`, `/myself` and `/organization`. Two deliberate non-defects were examined rather than "fixed": the brand slot renders `data-hcm-brand-logo-state="fallback"` with a `src`-less `` because `BrandLogoURL` is an administrator-supplied preference that is empty by default, and that image computes `display:none` at 0x0 so no broken-image icon or layout cost results while a `.sr-only` span still names the home link -- the REGRESSION test now forbids fabricating a default asset; and a `worker_self` searching their own name returns nothing because Person-kind results are gated on the People grant as a whole, which is consistent with being unable to browse any coworker, `myself` remaining reachable by its own search terms. One real latent weakness was found and left deliberately in place with coverage: `globalSearchItems` injects Help and Settings candidates unconditionally and relies entirely on `authorizedGlobalSearchItems` to strip them, a reliance invisible to any named-role test because every real role happens to hold `help`, so the zero-grant bundle stays first in the SECURITY matrix permanently. **Boundary.** The CSS cascade facts above -- computed `white-space`, `overflow-y`, `scrollbar-width` and real `scrollWidth`/`clientWidth` -- cannot be proven from a Go unit test; they are asserted only in the unexecuted Playwright spec, and the live run recorded here is what actually proves them

title: Offer the repair the journey names as its next step
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: journey `01a0b18f-94ce-7560-b01f-71a6af3b581b` shows the chip `Needs repair` and `Next step Governed repair`, while its Actions section offers only Withdraw (disabled), Request cancellation and Edit proposal; nothing on the page requests, tracks or explains a repair

refactor: expose the repair door through the same governed-action projection as pause, cancel and edit instead of an operator-only surface
evidence: fixed and verified live. The repair door already existed and is composed on every cell with an execution database (`composeWorkflowRepair`); what was missing was its projection -- the journey never said the repair exists, what it demands, who may authorize it, or what its fence can establish. `internal/intent/app/journey_repair.go` adds that projection: a new `REPAIR` intervention kind whose preview answers in the order a person would ask -- does this journey want a repair, can this deployment run one, may this viewer authorize one, is there a plan -- each with its own reason reference, because "no repair is needed", "this deployment cannot repair", "you are not authorized" and "no plan has been authored" are four different things to somebody trying to unstick a promotion. The requirements are read from `operator.PolicyFor(workflowcontrol.RepairKind)` rather than restated, so the page cannot describe a lighter action than the door enforces, and the authority question is put to **the same resolver the door itself consults** -- `composeWorkflowRepair` now returns it alongside the controller precisely so there is no second opinion about authority. `INDETERMINATE` is added to the shared outcome vocabulary and carried through as itself: a fence that could not establish whether the effect landed must not be reported as applied or denied. **The action is presented and never submittable from this page, and that is the finding's real shape rather than a shortcut.** A repair runs against an authored, simulated `RepairPlan` under a dual-controlled JIT grant; a promotion page holds none of that, and on this build the executor cannot run at all because none of its three external-system seams has a production adapter (the connectivity plane is read-only -- `composeWorkflowRepair`'s own doc says so). A button that always refused would be exactly the defect UXLIVE-011 removed from the target-position field, relocated. `RequestIntervention(REPAIR)` therefore refuses explicitly, naming the door and the grant, rather than forwarding a request with a plan this page would have had to invent. **Live proof** on the journey the RED names, `01a0b18f-94ce-7560-b01f-71a6af3b581b` (Isaac, `WRK-CO2 · P2 → WRK-MGR · M2`, chip `Needs repair`): its Actions section now leads with `Governed repair`, reading "A governed repair revalidates this journey's failed step against independently loaded current truth and, only if that still holds, drives one corrective effect behind an admission fence. The fence can answer that it could not establish whether the effect reached the external system, and that answer is reported as indeterminate rather than as success or failure. It requires a second approver distinct from whoever runs it, a simulation over exactly this scope and a current INTEGRITY_REPAIR grant.", refused with "You do not hold a current grant to authorize a governed repair." -- all three requirements supplied by the server's own preview. title: Stop re-downloading the whole UI bundle on every navigation
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: `journey.wasm` measures 38 598 KB decoded and 7 977 KB encoded, and `PerformanceResourceTiming.transferSize` reports about 7 978 KB on every workspace navigation with status 200 rather than 304, while `manifest.json`, `wasm_exec.js` and avatar images on the same origin report 0 or 304; the handler already sets `ETag`, gzip and `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, so revalidation is being defeated by the authenticated integrity fetch in the bootstrap script
green: a repeat navigation revalidates the bundle and transfers no body when it is unchanged, proven by transfer size and status in a browser run; the declared frontend performance budget names an explicit ceiling for bundle bytes on a repeat navigation and the gate fails when it is exceeded
refactor: use one bootstrap fetch contract for every asset — same credentials, integrity and cache semantics — instead of a separate path for the bundle
evidence: fixed and verified live. Two things were wrong, and the second only became visible after the first was fixed. (1) The asset address did not name the bytes, so no response could ever be kept: `internal/humanwork/workspace/handler.go` now answers a request whose `?v=` matches the asset's own sha256 with `private, max-age=31536000, immutable` and everything else with the previous `private, max-age=0, must-revalidate`, and both inline loaders (`render.go`, `journey_shell.go`) stamp the address from the manifest digest they already read. The digest is presentation only -- it never selects bytes, and a wrong value simply falls back to revalidation. (2) With that in place every addressed asset went to `transferSize` 0 on a repeat navigation **except the bundle**: measured in the browser, `harborcare-logo.svg` (1 010 B) and `wasm_exec.js` (16 992 B) were stored and reused under the identical policy while `journey.wasm` (8 181 669 B encoded) was re-transferred in full every time, including on a plain back-to-back double fetch of the same immutable URL. That is the HTTP cache's per-entry size cap, not a policy problem, and no header can talk a browser past it. So the loaders now keep the executable assets in the origin's own cache storage (`caches.open("hcmnext-assets")`), keyed by the addressed URL, storing only `r.ok` responses and dropping any entry for the same path under a different digest. The stored bytes were subresource-integrity-verified by the fetch that produced them, and the store is origin-private, so anything able to write it already runs in this origin. Setting `Content-Length` on asset responses is also part of this change (the bytes are whole in memory, and the response was going out chunked); it did not move the measurement on its own. **Live proof:** cold load of `/workspace/app/journeys` transferred 8 181 669 B for `journey.wasm` and stored both assets under their digests; navigating to `/workspace/app/people` -- a full document load -- produced **no `journey.wasm` or `wasm_exec.js` resource timing entry at all**, and the page still hydrated (title became `People · Harborcare Demo`, 64 people rendered). Before this change the same navigation reported `transferSize` 8 181 669 with status 200. **Tests:** `TestTodo_UXLIVE_013` (policy, the wrong-digest fallback, and a repeat-navigation budget of zero bundle bytes through a cache that obeys `Cache-Control`), `TestTodo_UXLIVE_013_Browser`, `TestTodo_UXLIVE_013_Golden`, `TestTodo_UXLIVE_013_Security`, `BenchmarkTodo_UXLIVE_013` (reports `bytes/nav`; 1 979 496 bytes/nav over 20 navigations, i.e. one transfer amortised, falling toward zero as the count rises). `go test ./internal/humanwork/workspace/ -count=1` passes (11.3s). **Three sibling contracts were co-evolved, not weakened:** `TestJourneyLoaderSourceIsTheDocumentedConstant` pins the loader byte for byte and was updated to the new bytes (its whole job is that the CSP hash and the source cannot drift, and the hash is derived from the source); `TestTodo_WEB_032_Conformance` and `TestTodo_WEB_033_Security` asserted the literal call sites `o(s.integrity)` / `o(a.integrity)`, which now read `k(...,s.integrity)` because the fetch moved inside the caching helper -- both now assert that `k` builds its options with `o(i)` and nothing else, and `web033` additionally rejects any `fetch(u,{` that would bypass it, so the guarantee they protect (no executable byte is fetched without both the bearer token and its SRI pin) is unchanged and slightly tighter

title: Return focus to the control that opened an overlay
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: the action launcher renders a dialog with `aria-haspopup="dialog"`, `aria-controls` and `aria-expanded` but wires no focus contract at all, so opening it leaves focus behind and dismissing it returns focus nowhere. (This todo was filed from a live observation that Escape on `Page utilities` left focus on the neighbouring `Language` summary; reading the code corrected that half -- the utility drawer does restore focus, and the measurement restored it to where focus actually was, because the drawer had been opened from a script rather than by its trigger.)
green: every dialog, popover and menu returns focus to its trigger on Escape, on a close control and on an outside dismissal; a keyboard test asserts the trigger is the active element after each dismissal path
refactor: implement dismissal and focus restoration once in the shared overlay primitive rather than per surface
evidence: the action launcher now uses the same focus contract as the utility drawer: `useDrawerFocusTrap("action-launcher-dialog", "action-launcher-trigger", open)` moves focus into the dialog when it opens and, on teardown, returns it to the element that opened it or to the trigger. It previously wired none, so a keyboard user who dismissed it resumed wherever focus had been left. `TestTodo_UXLIVE_020` (both dialogs wire the shared hook and the hook still restores to opener or trigger) and `_Browser` (a package-wide sweep: every `ID: "...-dialog"` in this package is wired to that hook, so a new overlay cannot ship without the contract) pass: `go test ./internal/humanwork/productui/ -count=1` ok on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). Limits: the restore itself is js/wasm-only (`drawer_focus_native.go` is a no-op on the test path), so these tests prove the wiring rather than the runtime behaviour, and the pane's synthetic key events do not reach the wasm handlers, so the keyboard round trip could not be measured live

title: Let only one row menu stand open at a time
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings

Re-measured, it does not: the boot resolves it. (The original observation waited three seconds; this bundle takes about ten to mount.)
