title: Let the organization tree use the width it was given
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: at a 1280 px viewport the unit list occupies roughly 430 px of a roughly 900 px card, leaving the right half empty while the `By team` and `Reporting lines` toggle floats alone at the far right
green: the tree uses the available card width at 1280 and 1440 px, with unit rows showing their counts and a second column or expanded rows for people; the view toggle sits with the content it controls; the layout stays legible at 768 and 375 px
refactor: lay the browser out with the shared density and column rules rather than a fixed-width list inside a wide card
evidence: the units use the column they are given. Root cause, found by measuring the live page: UIPOLISH-001's readable measure (`--hcm-measure-prose`, 65ch) applies to every `li` inside the shell, so each `.organization-unit` was capped at 583.05 px -- right for a sentence, wrong for a list item used as a layout container, and true of any structural list. `typed_mig_D.go` now releases it for the five known structural lists with `:is(.app-shell,.jn-embedded) :is(.metrics,.recent,.org-branches,.work-rows,.people-rows)>li { max-inline-size: none }`; the shell class is part of the selector because UIPOLISH-001's own `:is()` takes `.prose p`'s (0,1,1) and a bare `:is(classes)>li` ties with it and loses on source order. Verified live at 1440 x 900: the unit's computed `max-width` is `none` and it measures 1245 px in a 1245 px column, where it measured 583 px in an 886 px column. `TestTodo_UXLIVE_024` (the release exists and is scoped to direct children) and `_Browser` (it changes no typography) pass: `go test ./internal/humanwork/productui/ -count=1` ok on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). Limit: only those five lists are released; any other structural list still inherits the prose measure until it is named or the rule is inverted

title: Keep the application shell exactly one viewport tall
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: at 1280 × 800 with the Admin group expanded, `.app-shell` is 800 px but `document.documentElement.scrollHeight` is 996 px while `html` and `body` are `overflow: hidden`, so 196 px is unreachable; twice during the pass the document ended up scrolled (`scrollY` 82 and 324) with the global header at `top: -82` and no scrollbar to restore it
green: the document never exceeds the viewport while the shell owns its own scroll regions; a browser test asserts `documentElement.scrollHeight <= innerHeight` and `scrollY === 0` after expanding every navigation group, opening the longest disclosure on a journey and tabbing to the last sidebar destination, at 1280 × 800 and 1024 × 640
refactor: make the sidebar and main content the only scroll owners under the shell's explicit scroll-owner contract so no descendant can grow the document
evidence: the shell can no longer be scrolled away, and the cause was found rather than guessed. `overflow:hidden` on the root still creates a scroll container: measured on Brand & appearance at 1440 x 900, the root reported `scrollHeight` 1222 and `window.scrollTo(0, 500)` moved the document to 322 with the header at `top: -322` and no scrollbar to bring it back. The 322 px came from a `.sr-only` span inside `main` positioned `absolute` with `offsetParent` BODY: `main` is a scroll container but was not a containing block, so an absolutely positioned descendant resolved against the initial containing block, escaped the clip and extended the document. Two rules fix it: `html,body,#app` also declare `overflow:clip` (the `hidden` declaration stays as the fallback), and `.main,.main-scroll,.sidebar` declare `position:relative` so the scroll owners are containing blocks. Verified live on the same page: `documentElement.scrollHeight` is 900 against a 900 px viewport, and after `window.scrollTo(0, 500)` plus a direct `scrollTop` write `scrollY` is 0 with the header at `top: 0`. `TestTodo_UXLIVE_025` (the root is clipped, the fallback survives, the scroll owners are containing blocks) and `_Browser` (the real scroll owners and the print escape are intact) pass: `go test ./internal/humanwork/productui/ -count=1` ok on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). Limit: `overflow:clip` alone did not stop programmatic scrolling in this engine -- the containing-block rule is what removed the overflow -- so the clip is defence in depth rather than the fix

title: Decide intervention availability from the run, not from the assumption that blocked means unstarted
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: `InterventionAvailability` and its server twin treat `BLOCKED` as unstarted (`unstarted := stage == stageProposed || stage == stageBlocked`). On journey `01a0b189-e04c-7265-8926-909531dd6530`, whose finance and manager approvals both completed before revalidation refused, the page therefore offers Withdraw under the description `Stops this proposal before any approval has been recorded. No business effect has occurred.` and disables Cancel with `This proposal has not started its approval workflow yet. Use Withdraw instead of Cancel.` -- while the stepper directly above now shows both approvals completed
green: availability is decided from whether the run started and what it recorded, not from the stage alone, so a blocked-after-approval run offers the intervention that matches its real position and describes it truthfully; the client mirror and the server decision still agree over the full stage/kind cross product
refactor: keep one availability function shared by `internal/intent/app` and `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` and give it the run facts both already hold, rather than widening the stage vocabulary
evidence: availability is decided from the run, not from the assumption that blocked means unstarted. Both implementations now take a `started` fact: `interventionUnavailableAtStage(kind, stage, started)` in `internal/intent/app` (supplied by `detail.Instance != nil`) and `InterventionAvailability(kind, stage, started)` in `tools/uxqual/journeyclient` (supplied by `journeyStarted`, which reads the instance id the card already carries and the contract documents as empty before execution). Only BLOCKED depends on it: a blocked proposal that never started still offers Withdraw and refuses Cancel as before, while a blocked run whose approvals are recorded now refuses Withdraw with the already-started reason and offers Cancel, so the page no longer describes a run with recorded approvals as one where none were. `TestTodo_UXLIVE_026`, `_Browser` (the refused withdraw names the already-started reason) and `_Security` (every other stage's decision is unchanged by the new fact) pass, and `TestTodo_PROMOUX_013_ClientServerAvailabilityAgreement` now cross-checks the two implementations over every stage times both values of `started`: `go test ./internal/intent/app/ -count=1` ok (111.9s) and `go test ./tools/uxqual/journeyclient/ ./tools/uxqual/render/journey/ -count=1` leaves only the three failures another session's in-flight proto change already had, on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). Limit: this narrows one wrong offer and widens Cancel for blocked-after-start runs; the engine's own refusal remains the enforcement boundary for a cancel it will not accept

title: RESEARCH — Select an error-prevention and confirmation pattern for material promotion proposals
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings

green: research compares at least three established enterprise transaction-review patterns and tests them against promotion scenarios (ordinary, above-band, budget-shortfall, missing required values, changed/stale baseline and masked compensation); a reviewed decision recorded in this todo's Evidence names the chosen progressive-disclosure, validation-timing, warning-severity, confirmation-content, mobile and assistive-technology contract; executable golden fixtures encode that contract without submitting a promotion

title: Stop invalid promotion proposals before review and expose accessible field errors
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: selecting a role and position while leaving proposed base pay at `USD 0.00` and business reason empty still opens the review dialog with an enabled `Submit proposal`; the visible Cancel and Submit buttons have no accessible names in the live accessibility tree
green: the review action is unavailable until locally knowable required constraints pass; an attempted invalid review renders a summary plus inline messages, sets `aria-invalid` and `aria-describedby`, focuses the first invalid field and announces the error count; server refusals map through the same presentation contract; every review-dialog control has a stable accessible name and keyboard/focus behavior; no client check is treated as authority and the server still refuses forged invalid submissions
refactor: reuse the shared validation summary, field-error and modal-focus primitives for propose and edit; one typed refusal mapper serves SSR and Go/WASM paths

title: Make the promotion review a complete, decision-grade transaction summary
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: the live review modal shows only employee, role/grade transition and effective date; it omits target position, current and proposed base pay, exact and percentage delta, business reason, warnings and expected approval path even though those facts determine the transaction
green: review presents an authorization-filtered current-versus-proposed summary covering employee, role and grade, human position identity, organization and manager changes, exact currency/period base pay and delta, effective date, complete business reason, material warnings and the next approval owners or withheld equivalent; submit names the effect, the summary remains usable at 320 px and 200% zoom, and masked viewers never recover hidden facts from markup or accessible text
refactor: wire the existing `PromotionReview` and `CompensationGuardrailCard` projections into the production path and derive review facts from the canonical proposal candidate; do not recalculate compensation or authority in the renderer

title: Make target-position choices distinguishable and decisionable
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: Aya's proposal offers two radio choices that both read `Senior Data Engineer / Data & Analytics / Boston, MA / Open now — Available`; there is no visible position code, manager, reporting line, headcount type or other authorized discriminator
green: each option has a stable human label and only the authorized differentiating facts needed to choose it (position code or short id, manager/reporting context, location, headcount type and availability as applicable); genuinely indistinguishable duplicates are consolidated or explicitly explained; radio names, descriptions and selected state remain clear to assistive technology and in narrow layouts; selecting one binds its exact revision without trusting display text
refactor: extend the shared authorized vacancy projection and option-card component; do not perform a second position lookup or expose hidden workforce facts in the browser

title: Replace the zero-money default with safe exact-compensation entry
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: after the next role supplies a current salary and permitted band, Proposed base pay visibly defaults to `USD 0.00`; the screen makes a system-created zero look like a deliberate proposal and allows it to reach review
green: untouched compensation is represented as absent, never as floating point or an invented zero; the chosen product rule from `UXLIVE-034` either requires an explicit exact-money value or offers a clearly labelled suggestion derived by the compensation authority; currency and period stay attached, localized entry canonicalizes exactly, the live delta and band position update without becoming authority, and zero/out-of-range/ambiguous input cannot reach review
refactor: use the shared exact-money input and canonical decimal contract; suggestions come from the authorized compensation projection and remain distinguishable from user-confirmed values

title: Preserve promotion intent when choosing an employee
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: `Choose an employee to promote` navigates to the ordinary People directory without promotion eligibility enabled, so all 64 people appear, most rows end in `Unavailable`, and the user must discover and apply `Promotion eligible only` before continuing; the link also drops the current locale from its URL
green: the action opens a promotion-scoped, authorization-filtered employee selection state with eligibility already applied and clearly removable; result count, reason-neutral unavailable treatment, active-request continuation, search and Back behavior remain coherent; the canonical route preserves locale and other durable user preferences without encoding hidden eligibility facts; selecting a worker continues directly to that worker's proposal
refactor: encode task context through the shared route-state and person-workflow projection, reusing the People table rather than creating a second employee directory or filtering unauthorized rows in the client

title: Explain blocked, rejected and failed promotions from authoritative outcome evidence
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: a rejected request shows both approvals completed and says only that effective-date checks need attention; a failed request says to review its checks even though its only displayed check is informational; the blocked banner names only the band maximum while the same record also contains a budget shortfall
green: every blocked or terminal non-success state has one authoritative, localized reason summary derived from durable finding/outcome evidence, identifies the stage that stopped, distinguishes all contributing blocking findings from supplemental information and states the next permitted remediation or that none exists; the stage tracker, banner, outcome panel, history and list card cannot disagree; unauthorized details are withheld without changing the outer status shape
refactor: one outcome-reason projection consumes typed engine findings and terminal evidence for cards, detail and history; renderers do not infer causes from status strings or parse human messages

title: Make downstream-effect progress truthful, observable and time-bounded
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: Caleb is at `Checking downstream effects` with Proposal, Finance, Manager and Effective date complete and Recorded current, but `What happens next` says to complete remaining reviews; the page names no active final check, freshness, retry or threshold for concern
green: the page derives its next-step sentence from the current durable node/effect state, names the active downstream phase in business language, shows last progress and the next automatic action or bounded expectation, and changes to delayed/retrying/repair-required only from authoritative runtime evidence; a completed approval is never described as remaining; live-region updates are concise and do not continuously announce polling
refactor: project a typed progress summary from the workflow inspector and reuse it on journey detail, card and My Work; presentation does not poll provider internals or fabricate an ETA

title: Implement the researched status-first journey detail composition
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: active, waiting and terminal details render the same three-card Actions block before Stages; disabled actions and engine-oriented explanations occupy most of the first viewport while the current stage and outcome require scrolling
green: the page follows `UXLIVE-035`'s reviewed hierarchy; status, authoritative explanation, stage progress and the single useful next action appear first; destructive or rare interventions live in a clearly labelled secondary disclosure; terminal journeys omit irrelevant disabled cards and expose an outcome-appropriate follow-up; DOM/focus order matches visual order at desktop, 320/390 px, 200% zoom, German and RTL Arabic
refactor: compose shared status-summary, stage-tracker, primary-action and intervention-menu components from server-resolved facts; do not duplicate per-status layouts or client-side availability rules

title: Carry a human position identity from selection through review and history
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: the picker shows a human title, but journey comparison renders only UUIDs such as `70ae5423-59a9-55ba-abf3-00f495284b09`; `UXLIVE-003` removed the encoded revision token but its evidence explicitly records that the position title is still not carried by the proposal
green: the governed proposal binds the exact position revision and an immutable display snapshot sufficient to identify what the user chose; picker, review, journey comparison, history and exported evidence show the same authorized title plus stable short code/id; rename or later vacancy change does not rewrite the historical decision; unresolved or withheld identities render explicit safe states and never fall back to raw revision tokens outside diagnostics
refactor: define one position-identity value and authorized resolver at the workforce boundary; display snapshots support audit history while current live facts remain separately labelled

title: Use outcome-specific journey-card actions and progressive technical detail
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: every card uses `Open request`, including rejected and failed outcomes, and every card repeats a `Technical details` disclosure whether or not it helps the current task; next-step language is absent on terminal cards and generic on downstream processing
green: card action copy follows the authorized task state (`Review decision`, `Correct proposal`, `Complete approval`, `Track request` or equivalent from the shared vocabulary); the one next useful step is visible where one exists; implementation identifiers and diagnostics are absent from the default scan and available only through an authorized secondary path; accessible names include person, short reference, status and action without duplicating visible phrases
refactor: derive action label and next-step text from the same task/outcome projection used by detail and My Work; one shared diagnostics disclosure component owns technical metadata

title: Gate release on the complete promotion experience across success and recovery states
section: 74. September 17 live UI and UX audit findings
red: the individual promotion surfaces can each render while the real task still admits invalid review, loses task context, presents indistinguishable positions, contradicts runtime state or strands a user at a terminal result; no one gate traverses these seams with production components and a real store
green: against embedded PostgreSQL and the production Go/WASM client, persona-qualified scenarios cover promotion-scoped employee selection, exact-money entry, review, submit, finance and manager approval, effective-date waiting, downstream recording, completed outcome, blocked correction, rejection, failure and recovery; each asserts durable effects, authorized disclosure, focus/keyboard behavior, localized copy, route/scroll continuity, duplicate-submit fencing and the interaction-latency budget; desktop plus 390 px and 320 px live checks in light and dark are recorded in Evidence
refactor: reuse one seeded promotion-experience harness and shared page objects/projections; the gate observes public behavior and durable evidence rather than implementation-specific DOM structure or mock-only state

title: Disambiguate employee identity everywhere a person can be chosen or acted on
section: 72. September 14 live-UI regression findings
red: People rows, person headings, role assignments, global-search results or promotion actions identify a worker only as a first name; two same-named workers cannot be distinguished before opening or acting
green: every selection and action surface uses one authorized display-identity component with full permitted name plus stable worker number or equivalent disambiguator; withheld fields never leak, and accessible names identify the same worker as the visible label
refactor: extend the identity work of `UXAUDIT-016` through shared row, result and action props instead of formatting names independently on each page

title: Keep the action launcher focused on executable, scannable actions
section: 72. September 14 live-UI regression findings

green: the initial menu has a bounded, ranked action set and a clear employee-search path; ineligible matches are either omitted until specifically searched or shown once with one concise non-disclosing reason; keyboard focus and scrolling keep the chosen result visible
refactor: reuse the semantic-action projection and shared popover from `UXAUDIT-003`; do not create a second launcher inventory or eligibility rule

title: Make the global Promotion search result's destination truthful

green: an action-typed Promotion result leads to an authorized worker-selection/start step; a tracker destination is named and typed as a page; the two results have distinct descriptions and neither promises an unavailable action
refactor: derive result type, label and target from the same authorized action/page definitions used by the launcher and navigation

title: Compress Home's all-empty state around the next useful action

title: Execute real promotion steps through the capability gateway on the served path
section: 73. Workflow engine plan-vs-implementation gaps (2026-09-14)

refactor: delete the stub runner; one step-runner composition serves execute and simulate modes
evidence: a served promotion now commits and completes. Serve projects every `journey_worker` row into the DB-008/009/010 aggregates and seeds the promotion catalog (one job per published ladder job and grade, two OPEN vacancies per ladder target per organization unit, one compensation pool per unit) in the bootstrap transaction (`internal/data/demoworkforce/aggregates.go`), and `CreateWorker` projects its worker in the same transaction that inserts it. The propose path selects the OPEN target position deterministically and submits it as the picker-issued `position.RevisionRef` PROMOUX-004 re-derives existence, compatibility and vacancy from (`internal/intent/app/promotion_target_position.go`), carries the approved annualized base pay as a planned write in simcomp's own field path and pins the unchanged manager as an identical current/proposed assertion pair rather than a write (`proposal_commit_material.go`), and holds the raise against the unit's pool as a DB-010 `budget_reservation` recorded no later than the revision's `ProducedAt` (`internal/data/promotionbudget`), released by every terminal fact and by a governed cancellation. Each approval records its GOVERN-002 decision durably (migration 00309 `promotion_approval_governance`, append-only, tenant RLS: the composed `decision.Inputs`, the decision and its digest, the seven GOVERN-003 facts as the durable stores reported them, and the plan digest the decision authorized), built by the same construction `Revalidate` uses so an unchanged world reproduces the digest exactly. Limits: promotions of the fixed regression corpus (PROMO-EXEC-SERVE, PROMO-009, the PromoUX contract, UXAUDIT-002) still close `PROMOTION_BLOCKED`, because that population has no aggregate projection, target position or pool and its `manager_relationship_ref` names a relationship token rather than a worker, so its recorded approval denies on the budget and position facts — the real answer rather than a fabricated one; `simassign`/`simcomp` themselves are still not run on the served path (their snapshot needs six read ports with no production compensation or budget adapter, and their request needs the revision id and digest their own output would change), so their exported field-path and effect vocabulary is used instead; and the REFACTOR clause, one step-runner composition shared by execute and simulate, remains open

title: Classify authoritative core, downstream effects and derived updates
section: 73. Workflow engine plan-vs-implementation gaps (2026-09-14)
red: no node is classified AUTHORITATIVE_CORE, DOWNSTREAM_EFFECT or DERIVED_UPDATE, so a failed downstream effect can roll back or mask the authoritative outcome
green: the compiler requires the classification, the runtime commits the core independently, downstream failures route to reconciliation, and derived updates rebuild from the core

The runtime commits the authoritative core independently: when a dependent node fails, the advance transaction that records the attempt FAILED and moves the instance along its compiled failure route also inserts one sealed `workflow_effect_role_settlement` row (migration 00306, append-only, SELECT/INSERT, `forbid_mutation`) naming the failed node's role, effect class and effect key, the route it took (`RECONCILIATION` for a downstream effect, `REBUILD_FROM_CORE` for a derived update), the error class, the pinned plan digest and the core node executions that had already committed. The core's earlier commit is never touched or rolled back, and a failed downstream leg no longer either aborts the advance (leaving a RUNNING instance with nothing to run and the committed outcome masked behind an error) or refuses `NO_FAILURE_ROUTE`. `TestTodo_WF_RUN_037`, `_Property`, `_Fault` and `_Conformance` pass with the workflow, execute, runtime, platform/execution, promotionexec, simulate and conformance suites on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). title: Track bypass obligations and separate repair authority
section: 73. Workflow engine plan-vs-implementation gaps (2026-09-14)
red: no bypass obligation model, no overdue-review suspension, and no workflow.repair, override or migrate authority families; an approver can act as the repair operator
green: every bypass or break-glass records obligations with due review, overdue obligations suspend the capability, repair/override/migrate are distinct operator kinds, and approver and repair operator must differ

They are separate capability strings on a grant, so repair authority does not authorize an override. `internal/intent/operator/obligation.go` adds the digest-sealed `Obligation` (kind, family, scope, operator, approver of record, authority used, what was bypassed and why, `DueAt = RecordedAt + 24h`) and the `ObligationStore` port; `Gateway.Submit` loads the tenant's outstanding obligations before any authority is spent and refuses `OPERATOR_OBLIGATION_OVERDUE` for a suspended family and `OPERATOR_REPAIR_SEPARATION` when a repair-family operator is an approver of record over an overlapping scope, which is the durable half of "approver and repair operator must differ". A bypass with no store to record it is refused `OPERATOR_OBLIGATION_STORE_REQUIRED`, a store write failure aborts the pending receipt before the executor runs, and an unreadable store fails the submission closed. `Gateway.ReviewObligation` discharges only for a reviewer who is neither the operator nor the approver. Migration 00310 `operator_bypass_obligation` carries a foreign key to `operator_control_receipt`, RLS `tenant_isolation`, a partial outstanding index, no DELETE grant with `forbid_mutation` on DELETE, and a review-only UPDATE trigger that permits exactly one transition; a stored row whose content no longer matches its sealed digest is refused. `internal/capability` gains `SuspensionSource`, `WithSuspensions` and `CAPABILITY_SUSPENDED`, checked right after version resolution and before authorization so no scope or envelope can talk past a suspension, satisfied structurally by `operator.CapabilitySuspensions` (failing closed on an unreadable store or an unnameable tenant) with no import in either direction. `TestTodo_WF_RUN_039`, `_Security`, `_Mutation`, `_Suspension` and `_Recovery` (an obligation recorded before a restart is still outstanding and still suspending afterwards; discharge is once-only; tenants isolated) pass with `internal/intent/operator` 96.4%, `internal/capability` 91.9%, `internal/data/operatorjournal` 83.4% and `internal/intent/operator/workflowcontrol` 91.3% on windows/arm64 (Go 1.26.3). Limits: the served cell builds one cell-wide capability gateway that carries no tenant, so it is not yet handed a tenant-resolved suspension source (the operator gateway's own suspension is live in production through the journal auto-wire); and the durable separation rule reads approvers of record from outstanding obligations only, not from every dual-control receipt
